myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: The aim of the study was to evaluate the 2-year real-world effectiveness of diffusion optics technology (DOT) spectacle lenses for pediatric myopia control in Chinese clinical practice. METHODS: This retrospective real-world comparative study analyzed patient records from children prescribed DOT or single-vision (SV) spectacle lenses. Sequential 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) was performed for the year-1 and year-2 analyses, respectively: The first PSM matched baseline characteristics of the two groups; the second PSM re-matched the DOT group's year-1 characteristics against the SV group's baseline characteristics. Primary outcomes were changes in cycloplegic spherical equivalent (SE) and axial length (AL). myopia.summary: Over 24 months, ChT showed a region-specific treatment response, most consistent temporally, less consistent nasally, and subfoveally. Regional ChT may offer an exploratory marker of treatment-related remodelling, but its predictive value for individualised treatment remains uncertain.

We evaluated regional choroidal responses to adding. Defocus Incorporated Multiple Segments (DIMS) spectacles to 0.025% atropine, and asessed biomarker potential of regional and baseline ChT. METHODS: This secondary analysis included ASPECT participants with enhanced-depth imaging OCT scans. myopia.title: Effects of orthokeratology lens wear on myopia progression and axial elongation in children: a 1:1 age-matched retrospective study.
myopia.summary: Orthokeratology is associated with slower myopia progression in children compared with age-matched controls. However, its effect on axial elongation is less consistent with no significant difference in the rate of axial elongation. No clear difference is observed in myopia control efficacy between lens types.
myopia.abstract: AIM: To evaluate the effects of orthokeratology lens wear on myopia progression and axial elongation in children using a 1:1 age-matched design and to compare outcomes according to lens type. METHODS: This retrospective study included 1854 children (3708 eyes) who wore orthokeratology lenses between April 2019 and January 2026 and 1854 age-matched controls (3708 eyes) who did not receive myopia-control treatment at a single institution. Controls were matched 1:1 by age within ±1mo. Spherical equivalent (SE) and axial length (AL) were measured at 6-month intervals for up to 36mo. Annual rates of change were estimated using linear mixed-effects models, excluding baseline for SE and including baseline for AL. myopia.title: Visual field performance of the novel DIMS TED spectacle lens compared with DIMS and single-vision spectacle lenses.
myopia.summary: The DIMS TED spectacle lens was associated with no clinically meaningful reduction in visual field sensitivity within the central 30° compared with DIMS and SV spectacle lenses in myopic children. This finding supports the visual tolerability of this intensified defocus design for childhood myopia management. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the visual field performance of DIMS TED spectacle lens, an enhanced Defocus Incorporated Multiple Segments (DIMS) spectacle lens design featuring more defocus segments closer to the geometric center, higher defocus power and extended defocus treatment zone, compared with DIMS and single vision (SV) spectacle lenses. METHODS: Children aged 9 to 14 years with cycloplegic spherical equivalent refractive error (SER) ranged from -1.00 to -6.00D were recruited. Visual field performance was assessed using an automated static perimeter (Zeiss, Humphrey Visual Field HFA 750i) with SITA Fast 30-2 protocol. A Goldmann size III (0.43o) green flashing stimulus of varying luminance levels was presented at 76 random test points within 30o visual field. myopia.title: Age-Related Post-Discontinuation Refractive and Axial Length Changes After Tapered 0.125% Atropine Therapy.
myopia.summary: Post-discontinuation myopic progression and axial elongation were substantially greater in patients who stopped atropine at age 12 than in those who stopped at age 13 or older. These findings suggest that age, refractive stability, and axial length trend should be considered when planning discontinuation of low-dose atropine therapy.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate age-related refractive and axial length changes after tapered discontinuation of 0.125% atropine in children and adolescents treated for myopia control. METHODS: This retrospective study reviewed records of 256 patients aged 12 to 16 years who received 0.125% a standardized tapering protocol before discontinuation. Tapering consisted of nightly bilateral instillation reduced to every-other-night for 4 weeks, then twice-weekly for 4 weeks, then complete cessation. Patients with at least 12 months of follow-up after discontinuation were included. Spherical equivalent (SE) progression and axial length (AL) change were compared among five age groups (12-16 years) using Welch's analysis of variance and Pearson correlation. myopia.title: Achieving natural eye and lens interaction based eyeglasses optical fit through a parametric customization approach.
myopia.summary: Eyeglasses are widely used to correct refractive errors, but optical fit evaluation usually emphasizes lens design alone and mainly assumes uniform use of the lens aperture. This can increase design complexity and cost while overlooking how the eye interacts with the lens during everyday wear. …
myopia.abstract: Eyeglasses are widely used to correct refractive errors, but optical fit evaluation usually emphasizes lens design alone and mainly assumes uniform use of the lens aperture. This can increase design complexity and cost while overlooking how the eye interacts with the lens during everyday wear. Here we show that favorable eyeglasses optical fit can be achieved through head-anthropometry-based parametric frame customization within the context of natural eye and lens interaction. We combined parametric frame design with mathematical lens modeling and evaluated both myopia and presbyopia groups. The results show that appropriate frame customization can maintain rational control of oblique aberrations for spherical and basic aspheric lenses without relying on high-order lens terms. myopia.title: Deep learning model for risk assessment of myopic progression in children wearing orthokeratology lenses.
myopia.summary: The HAM, developed from routine ocular examinations and questionnaires, can rapidly identify patients at high risk of rapid myopia progression. Its high performance and temporal validation enhance the reliability. …
myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: To construct a risk stratification model for axial length elongation in orthokeratology lenses, facilitating the identification of high-risk patients. METHOD: This study collected case data on Ortho-K lenses at the Ophthalmology Department and Optometry Center of Peking University People's Hospital from January 2018 to May 2021. The Ortho-K cohort used for model development included 1,639 myopia patients (3,271 eyes), and the cohort of 216 patients (356 eyes) collected at different times was used for temporal verification. Hierarchical Attention Model (HAM) based on the transformer was trained, and performance was assessed for validation temporally. The HAM was designed based on attention mechanism, which could be embedded into each feature group independently, and combined with local and global attention mechanisms to deal with complex interactions in medical data. myopia.title: Low-Concentration Atropine Eye Drops in Children With Myopia and Intermittent Exotropia: The AMIXT2 Randomized Clinical Trial.
myopia.summary: In the AMIXT2 randomized clinical trial among children with myopia and IXT, 0.04% atropine eye drops were associated with less myopia progression and axial elongation over 12 months than 0.01% or 0.02% atropine eye drops. …
myopia.abstract: IMPORTANCE: The optimal atropine concentration for myopia control in children with coexisting intermittent exotropia (IXT) remains uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To compare the efficacy and safety of 0.01%, 0.02%, and 0.04% atropine eye drops in children with myopia and IXT. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This single-center, double-masked, 3-arm randomized clinical trial was conducted from September 2023 to March 2026. Children aged 6 to 12 years with basic-type IXT and myopia (cycloplegic spherical equivalent [SE], -0.50 to -6.00 diopters [D]) were enrolled. Data analysis was conducted from March 2026 to July 2026. INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomized 1:1:1 to 0.01%, 0.02%, or 0.04% atropine eye drops nightly in both eyes. myopia.title: Research Progress and Safety Controversies of Repeated Low-Level Red Light Therapy for Myopia Prevention and Control.
myopia.summary: In recent years, the global prevalence of myopia has continued to rise. Complications associated with high myopia have become important risk factors for vision impairment, underscoring the need to identify safe and effective strategies for myopia prevention and control. …
myopia.abstract: In recent years, the global prevalence of myopia has continued to rise. Complications associated with high myopia have become important risk factors for vision impairment, underscoring the need to identify safe and effective strategies for myopia prevention and control. Repeated low-level red light (RLRL) therapy, an emerging nonpharmacological intervention, has shown potential to slow axial elongation and mitigate myopia progression. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in RLRL research. Starting from the physical properties of red light, we outline putative mechanisms, including activation of mitochondrial metabolism, modulation of dopamine and nitric oxide signaling, and structural responses such as choroidal thickening and scleral remodeling. We further synthesize evidence on efficacy and parameter optimization from animal models and randomized controlled clinical st

myopia.summary: RLRL showed the largest estimated effects and ranked highest among the evaluated interventions for one-year control of pediatric high myopia, while PSR, RGP, and orthokeratology also showed potential benefits. …
myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: High myopia in children and adolescents is a growing public health concern associated with increased risk of irreversible vision impairment. Identifying the most effective and safe intervention to slow its progression is critical. METHODS: We searched PubMed, EMBASE, Scopus, Cochrane Library, ClinicalTrials.gov, and WHO ICTRP for randomized controlled trials and observational studies (NOS score ≥ 6 or low/moderate ROBINS-I bias risk) published until March 16, 2025. Twelve interventions were evaluated. PRIMARY OUTCOMES: annual change in refractive error (D/year) and axial length (mm/year). SECONDARY OUTCOMES: adverse events. Random-effects pairwise and network meta-analyses were performed. myopia.summary: Spectacle dependence, particularly for moderate-to-high myopia, represents a significant marksmanship liability. On precision rifles, optics and night-vision devices act as coupled performance multipliers while CBRN degrade scores because of cheek-weld interference. …
myopia.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Vision is a critical component of military readiness, yet nearly 25% of U.S. service members require spectacle correction. This study quantitatively investigated the impact of spectacle-corrected refractive error, particularly myopia, alongside modern operational variables (assisted night fire, Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear [CBRN] protective mask, and optical assistance) on individual weapon qualification performance. myopia.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Compare the effectiveness of three different optical microstructure lens designs-defocus- incorporated multiple segments (DIMS), highly aspherical lenslets (HAL), and diffusion optics technology (DOT)-in controlling myopia progression in children. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study collected clinical data from myopic children wearing microstructure-designed spectacle lenses who visited West China Hospital of Sichuan University, Wuhou West China Likang Optometry Clinic, Meishi Kang Eye Optometry Center, and Chengdu Xiaoai Eye Clinic for refraction and follow-up between May 2024 and December 2025. myopia.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the comorbidity rates of myopia, overweight and obesity, and spinal curvature abnormalities among primary and secondary school students in Chengdu in 2024, explore the influencing factors of comorbidity, and provide a scientific basis for developing comorbidity prevention and control strategies for common diseases in this population. METHODS: A stratified cluster random sampling method was employed. Primary and secondary school students from 23 districts under the jurisdiction of Chengdu were randomly selected as study subjects in 2024. Physical examinations and questionnaire surveys were conducted to analyze the comorbidity rates of myopia, overweight and obesity, and spinal curvature abnormalities. myopia.title: Similar annualized axial length elongation with 5.0-mm and 6.0-mm back optic zone diameter (BOZD) orthokeratology lenses in children and adolescents: a retrospective real-world analysis.
myopia.summary: In this real-world setting, no statistically significant difference in annual AL elongation (~0.20 mm/year) was detected between the 5.0-mm and 6.0-mm BOZD CRT lenses. Both groups exhibited elongation rates approaching the physiological levels observed in emmetropic children.
myopia.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the comparative effectiveness of 5.0-mm versus 6.0-mm back optic zone diameter (BOZD) orthokeratology (ortho-K) lenses of the CRT design in controlling axial length (AL) elongation among Chinese children and adolescents, given the scarcity of real-world evidence and the predominantly controlled nature of previous investigations. METHODS: This retrospective, real-world, single-center investigation included Chinese children aged 7 to 16 years who underwent corneal refractive therapy (CRT) with ortho-K lenses, with a BOZD of either 5.0 mm or 6.0 mm, from May 2018 to August 2023, with follow-up extending until June 2025. The principal outcome was annual AL elongation (mm/year), derived from initial and subsequent measurements. myopia.abstract: Low-dose atropine (0.01%) is widely used for pediatric myopia control, yet its effect on light-related visual discomfort under real-world lighting remains uncertain. We assembled a clinic-based observational cohort of 120 adolescents (12-18 years; myopia -3.00 to -6.00 D spherical equivalent) and compared 69 atropine users with 51 non-atropine controls. The primary outcome was a validated 0-10 visual discomfort composite score (Visual Discomfort Scale, VDS-10), administered under standardized ambient conditions (300 lx, 5000 K), with secondary measures including glare threshold (cd/m2; C-Quant, Oculus GmbH), pattern-glare score (Wilkins/Evans protocol), photopic and mesopic pupil diameters (PLR-200, NeurOptics), reading speed, and ambient lighting logged via wearable spectroradiometric sensors (Sekonic C-800). myopia.title: Five-year efficacy and safety of repeated low-level red light therapy for myopia control in children: a multicenter, real-world study.
myopia.summary: In this large real-world cohort with follow-up of up to 5 years, RLRL therapy was associated with sustained AL control and no serious safety signals based on available clinical records. These findings support its potential role as a long-term myopia management strategy.
myopia.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Repeated low-level red light (RLRL) therapy has emerged as a promising intervention for pediatric myopia control; however, large-scale evidence on its long-term efficacy and safety remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the sustained effectiveness and safety of RLRL therapy in children and adolescents with myopia. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included patients aged 3-17 years who received RLRL therapy for at least 1 year across 12 clinical sites, with follow-up extending up to 5 years. The primary efficacy outcome was effective axial length (AL) control, defined as annual AL elongation <0.1 mm, assessed from years 1-5. Safety outcomes included the proportions of patients with a ≥2-line reduction in best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) or BCVA worse than 20/25. RESULTS: A total of 2885 patients were included. myopia.title: Myopia Frequency and Associated Factors Among Children and Adolescents Attending Tertiary Eye-Care Centers in Iraq: A Multicenter Study.
myopia.summary: The observed 60.1% myopia frequency applies to this selected tertiary-care sample and is not a population prevalence estimate for Iraqi youth. Older age, parental myopia, urban residence, and lower outdoor exposure were associated with myopia, while axial length was the strongest concurrent biometric correlate of SE.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To quantify the frequency of myopia and examine demographic, behavioral, and ocular biometric correlates in a selected tertiary-care sample of Iraqi children and adolescents. METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter, cross-sectional comparative study included 6-18-year-olds examined during 2023-2025 at three tertiary eye care centers. Cycloplegic autorefraction and optical biometry were performed. Myopia was defined as right-eye spherical equivalent (SE) ≤-0.50 D. Multivariable logistic regression was used to evaluate factors associated with myopia, and linear regression was used to evaluate concurrent correlates of SE. RESULTS: Among 6,356 participants, 3,820 (60.1%) were myopic and 2,536 (39.9%) emmetropic. The frequency and severity of myopia increased with age. Method: Children aged 4-16 years, who were started on Atropine 0.025% with at least 6 months of follow-up, were included. A total of 588 eyes (299 children) were classified as treatment-naïve eyes started on Atropine 0.025% daily (Group A, n146), eyes progressing on Atropine 0.01% daily increased to 0.025% daily (Group B, n287) or combined with myopia control glasses (Group C, n66), and those stable on Atropine 0.01% twice daily converted to Atropine 0.025% daily (Group D, n89). Spherical equivalent (SE) and axial length (AL) were recorded from 6 months before treatment to 24 months after treatment began. myopia.summary: Background: Myopia is a major public health challenge, particularly among children, with prevalence increasing worldwide. Emerging light-based interventions, including low-level red light (LLRL) and short-wavelength light therapy, may be effective for myopia control. …
myopia.abstract: Background: Myopia is a major public health challenge, particularly among children, with prevalence increasing worldwide. Emerging light-based interventions, including low-level red light (LLRL) and short-wavelength light therapy, may be effective for myopia control. This systematic review aimed to assess the effectiveness and safety of LLRL and short-wavelength light therapy for myopia control in children. Methods: A systematic search was performed in PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, Google Scholar, and EBSCO in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Studies published between 2013 and 2026 assessing the effectiveness and safety of LLRL and short-wavelength therapies for myopia control were included. The review examined whether early optical measurements of the lens-eye system can provide clinically useful prediction of later axial growth. …
myopia.abstract: Background: Contact-lens interventions can slow, but do not arrest, axial elongation in children, and individual response varies substantially. The review examined whether early optical measurements of the lens-eye system can provide clinically useful prediction of later axial growth. Methods: A critical narrative review of PubMed-indexed literature was updated through October 2026. Evidence from dual-focus, centre-distance multifocal and extended-depth-of-focus soft contact lenses and orthokeratology was appraised according to temporal ordering, repeatability, independent prediction, external validation and potential clinical utility. myopia.title: Auricular acupressure combined with defocus spectacle lenses for myopia control in children with unilateral myopia: A retrospective study.
myopia.summary: Auricular acupressure combined with defocus spectacle lenses yields favorable myopia control and preventive effects for both the myopic eye and the fellow non-myopic eye in children with unilateral myopia.
myopia.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate refractive and axial length (AL) changes associated with auricular acupressure combined with defocus spectacle lenses in the myopic and fellow non-myopic eyes of children with unilateral myopia. METHODS: Clinical data from 60 children (120 eyes) diagnosed with unilateral myopia between June 2024 and September 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. The children ranged in age from 6 to 15 years (mean, 10.02 ± 1.79 years). All children received auricular acupressure combined with defocus spectacle lenses for myopia control. Spherical equivalent (SE), cylindrical power, AL, and changes in these parameters over 6 months were recorded. RESULTS: At baseline and after 6 months of treatment, the SE of the myopic eye was -1.00 (-1.75, -0.88) D and -1.25 (-1.84, -0.88) D, respectively, with no statistically significant difference. myopia.title: Intrapupillary Functional Zone Distribution and Axial Elongation During Orthokeratology.
myopia.summary: Intrapupillary functional zone distribution, particularly PFZ, provided more incremental explanatory information about 12-month axial elongation than mean PR alone. These contemporaneous associations warrant prospective validation before use in prediction or lens optimisation.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate associations of intrapupillary functional zone distribution and corneal curvature changes with 12-month axial elongation during orthokeratology (OK). METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 276 eyes of children and adolescents wearing corneal refractive therapy-designed OK lenses. Baseline and 12-month corneal topography were used to quantify intrapupillary treatment (PFZ), defocus (PSZ) and residual (POZ) areas, together with zone-specific curvature changes. Pupil radius (PR) was averaged across the two visits; zone areas were defined using the 12-month pupil boundary. Spearman correlation and hierarchical linear regression assessed associations with 12-month axial elongation. myopia.title: Normal corneal endothelial development is preserved during pediatric daily disposable omafilcon A soft contact lens wear.
myopia.summary: These findings are consistent with daily disposable omafilcon A soft contact lens wear not altering the normal age-related trajectory of corneal endothelial change in children and support preservation of the endothelial structure during pediatric contact lens use.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: Corneal health during pediatric soft contact lens wear remains an important consideration in myopia management. This study evaluated longitudinal changes in endothelial cell density (ECD) and morphology in children participating in the Japan MiSight 1 day clinical trial. METHODS: A total of 60 subjects (mean age 10.4 ± 1.3 years at baseline) contributed 470 longitudinal endothelial measurements over 2 years. All subjects were wearing daily disposable omafilcon A soft contact lenses, including the dual focus MiSight 1 day myopia control and single vision Proclear 1 day designs. Subjects underwent specular microscopy measurements and data were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. myopia.title: Repeated low-level red light therapy for childhood myopia management.
myopia.summary: RLRL therapy is an effective intervention for slowing myopia progression in children, with longer follow-up duration associated with greater efficacy. However, its safety profile still requires further validation.
myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: Myopia has emerged as a major global public health challenge, with an urgent need for effective treatment strategies. Repeated low-level red light (RLRL) therapy has recently gained attention as a promising approach, with an increasing number of meta-analyses revealing its efficacy in myopia management. Therefore, we conducted the umbrella review to illustrate the overall evidence landscape, assess the reliability of previous studies, and identify potential evidence gaps of RLRL therapy for myopia control in children. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane Library, CNKI, Wanfang, Epistemonikos and Web of Science up to 13 February 2026. Systematic reviews and meta-analyses primarily comparing RLRL with single-vision spectacles in myopic children were eligible. METHODS: A cross-sectional questionnaire-based survey was conducted among eye care practitioners across India between November 2025 and February 2026. The survey assessed perceived challenges, barriers, and strategies related to Ortho-K practice using a five-point Likert scale. Responses were summarized using frequencies, percentages, and medians with interquartile ranges (IQRs). Differences in domain scores according to Ortho-K exposure were analyzed using the Kruskal-Wallis test, whereas correlations between domains were evaluated using Spearman rank correlation. myopia.title: Efficacy and safety of repeated low-level red light therapy in myopia control: an updated and comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis.
myopia.summary: This meta analysis suggests that, in the short term (within 12 months of follow up), RLRL may be associated with slower axial length elongation, less myopic refractive progression, and increased choroidal thickness in children with myopia. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aims to assess the therapeutic effectiveness and safety of repeated low-level red light for myopia management in children and adolescents. METHODS: Multiple databases were systematically searched for studies evaluating the efficacy of RLRL in myopia control among children and adolescents. Data were extracted and analyzed using RevMan 5.4. The primary outcomes included axial length (AL), spherical equivalent refraction (SER), and subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT), while secondary outcomes included corneal curvature (K1, K2) and anterior chamber depth (ACD). RESULTS: A total of 19 studies were included. This study employed meta-analysis and subgroup analyses to evaluate the efficacy and to explore heterogeneity based on intervention duration and myopia severity. myopia.title: Current Optical Correction and Presenting Vision Among Schoolchildren With Vision Screening-identified Myopia in Yangzhou, China.
myopia.summary: Approximately one-third of students with vision screening-identified myopia had no recorded correction. Screening reports should identify both the use of correction and the presenting visual outcomes. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To describe the current optical correction and present visual outcomes of schoolchildren identified with myopia during vision screening. METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis was conducted of data from 12,106 students aged 6.0-18.99 years in 36 schools in Yangzhou, China. Vision screening-identified myopia was defined using visual acuity (VA) and noncycloplegic refraction; current orthokeratology users were also included. VA is reported in five-mark notation with logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution (logMAR) equivalents. myopia.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Myopia is becoming an epidemic among children globally, due to increased near screen exposure and reduced outdoor activity. Health advocacy-actions designed to gain political commitment, policy support, and social acceptance for health goals-can help to address this public health challenge. This paper reflects on health advocacy activities undertaken to contain the myopia epidemic and on potential future directions. METHODS: We mapped activities using the American Heart Association (AHA) advocacy framework undertaken in the Netherlands from 2018 to 2026 via the innovative multidisciplinary network 'View Outdoors' (2018), targeting professionals, policymakers, and the public. METHODS: This cohort study enrolled 4227 mother-child pairs with children aged 3-6 years, and incorporated both a prospective analysis and a nested case-control analysis as its sub-studies. METHODS: A Markov cohort model simulated myopia progression over 10 years in children starting treatment at 8 years of age. Cost-effectiveness was evaluated using the incremental cost-utility ratio (ICUR) and incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER), measured as cost per quality-adjusted life year (QALY) gained and cost per disability-adjusted life year (DALY) averted, respectively. Deterministic and probabilistic sensitivity analyses assessed model robustness. If an intervention exhibited sensitivity or instability, its cost-effectiveness cannot be determined conclusively within the range of parameter variations. myopia.summary: Children undergoing orthokeratology showed a mean one-year axial elongation of 0.23 mm. Older age, higher baseline myopia, larger pupil diameter and BMI were associated with axial elongation during treatment, with notable sex differences. These findings may help inform individualized orthokeratology management in pediatric myopia.

This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of orthokeratology (Ortho-K) in controlling axial length (AL) elongation in myopic children over a one-year period and to identify baseline predictors of treatment response. METHODS: This retrospective, single-group, pre-post control study included 122 children (244 eyes) with myopia who were fitted with orthokeratology lenses at Jiangyin People's Hospital between January 2024 and December 2025 and completed one year of follow-up. myopia.title: Effectiveness of spectacle lenses with highly aspherical lenslets (HAL) in slowing axial elongation and spherical equivalent refraction progression in myopic and pre-myopic children: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
myopia.summary: Current evidence suggests that HAL spectacle lenses may slow axial elongation and SER progression in myopic children. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, VIP, and WanFang databases were systematically searched from inception to June 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCT) and prospective cohort studies comparing HAL lenses with single-vision lenses (SVL) for myopia control or prevention were included. Two investigators independently screened literature, extracted data, and assessed the risk of bias. Meta-analysis was performed using RevMan 5.4 software. myopia.title: Trends in real-world atropine prescribing for myopia control across evidence eras.
myopia.summary: A clear shift in atropine prescribing patterns for pediatric myopia management was identified over the course of the study period. During the Early Low-Dose Atropine Era, clinicians exclusively prescribed the lowest concentration of atropine (0.01%), and only a small proportion of patients were escalated to a higher concentration at 12 mo …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: Identify trends in atropine prescribing and concentration adjustments for pediatric myopia control across multiple U.S. academic eye centers. METHODS: A multicenter, retrospective chart review was conducted of children (ages 3-17 years) prescribed low-concentration atropine for myopia management at three academic medical centers in the United States: the Casey Eye Institute, Oregon Health & Science University, the Ann & Robert H. Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago, and the Rady Children's Hospital Orange County. Descriptive statistics were used to characterize the data and summarize prescribing patterns, concentration changes, and follow-up rates by enrollment period and initial atropine concentration. myopia.title: Variations in Corneal Refractive Change Region After Orthokeratology Lens Wear.
myopia.summary: Orthokeratology induces measurable changes in the height and volume of the CRC region. Both parameters are important for evaluating myopia control outcomes, and our findings provide guidance for clinical lens selection.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: This study analyzed 1-year longitudinal variations in the corneal refractive change (CRC) region after orthokeratology (Ortho-K) lens wear between vision shaping treatment (VST) and corneal refractive therapy (CRT) designs. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 148 patients with myopia (148 eyes) treated with Ortho-K lenses for 12 months at Beijing Tongren Hospital's myopia clinic from June 2020 to December 2022. Participants were divided into two groups: group A (74 eyes) who wore VST design Ortho-K lens, and group B (74 eyes) who wore CRT design lens. Data from the right eyes were collected. Measurements included tangential corneal topography maps, which were converted into refractive power maps to calculate the area, height, and volume of the CRC region. myopia.summary: The evaluated contact lenses showed good short-term performance and tolerance. A smaller central optical zone was associated with modest reductions in contrast sensitivity and perceived visual quality, without clear advantages in other outcomes. Hydration modality did not influence performance.

METHODS: Thirty myopic young adults (21 ± 1 years) were fitted monocularly with three centre-distance multifocal designs: 3.9 mm optical zone with bulk hydration, 3.9 mm with blister hydration, and 3.6 mm with bulk hydration. A no-contact lens condition served as baseline. High-contrast visual acuity (CDVA) and contrast sensitivity function (CSF) under photopic and mesopic conditions, tear film parameters (tear meniscus heigh, non-invasive tear break-up time), and Likert scales (visual quality, comfort, satisfaction) were assessed using a repeated-measures design. myopia.title: Systematic review of atropine cost-effectiveness in childhood myopia management.
myopia.summary: Studies demonstrate favourable economic value using diverse metrics, including cost per diopter reduction, cost ratios, and cost-utility estimates, rather than uniformly reported ICERs. …
myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: Childhood myopia is a global public health concern, with rising prevalence and a significant economic burden due to complications like retinal detachment and macular degeneration. Low-dose atropine (LDA) range 0.01%-0.05% is a clinically effective intervention for slowing myopia progression. However, its economic value remains under-evaluated across diverse settings. METHODS AND FINDINGS: We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251009680) to assess the cost-effectiveness of atropine for myopia management in children. Four model-based economic evaluations met the inclusion criteria, from Hong Kong, New Zealand, Australia/China and France/United Kingdom. myopia.title: Twelve-Month Efficacy and Visual Tolerability of MyoPi Spectacle Lenses in Childhood Myopia: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
myopia.summary: In children with myopia, MyoPi continuous free-form defocus spectacle lenses slowed 12-month axial elongation and cycloplegic refractive progression compared with single-vision spectacles, with acceptable overall safety and visual tolerability.
myopia.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the 12-month efficacy, safety, and visual tolerability of MyoPi continuous free-form defocus spectacle lenses compared with conventional single-vision spectacle lenses (SVLs) in children with myopia. DESIGN: Prospective, multicenter, randomized, single-masked, parallel-group clinical trial. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 116 eligible children were randomized 1:1 to MyoPi or SVLs. Eligible participants were 8 to 13 years of age with bilateral cycloplegic spherical equivalent refraction (SER) from -0.75 to -5.00 diopters (D). METHODS: Participants were randomized 1:1 to MyoPi or single-vision spectacle lenses and were followed at baseline, week 1, month 3, month 6, and month 12. METHODS: This was a retrospective study conducted on school-age children with myopia of -5.00 D or higher who were fitted with DRGP lenses. A matched control group wearing single-vision (SV) spectacles was selected based on comparable baseline age and refractive error. The AL was measured at baseline and at 6-month intervals thereafter. Changes in AL were compared between the groups. RESULTS: The DRGP lenses group comprised 56 subjects (39 females, mean age 11.96±2.32y), the SV spectacle group comprised 53 subjects (29 females, mean age 11.09±2.33y). myopia.summary: The study constructs a risk prediction model to forecast the likelihood that myopic adolescents will not achieve the ideal control effect after wearing OK lenses, offering proactive and effective guidance for frontline clinical practitioners in devising diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis of myopic children who used OK lenses consistently for at least 18mo between January 2021 and March 2023 were conducted. Various ophthalmic examinations and recorded baseline parameters were performed. A risk prediction model was developed using multifactorial logistic regression analysis, and the model's discrimination and calibration were assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and Brier score. RESULTS: The modeling group included 228 eyes (mean age, 10.46±1.99y; 55.7% males), with 120 right eyes (52.6%) and 108 left eyes (47.4%), and the validation group included 100 eyes. myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: Myopia is a worldwide health concern due to its increasing prevalence and associated pathology, visual dysfunction, societal and quality of life impacts. Despite widespread use of atropine in Taiwan to manage myopia, its prevalence has increased. It has been suggested that the efficacy of atropine in slowing myopia progression may be limited by binocular vision (BV) function. Furthermore, the long-term impacts of atropine are unknown. This study aimed to contrast the BV profile of young myopic adults following cessation of atropine therapy for myopia control, relative to myopic adults without this history. METHODS: A total of 1,142 children (527 in urban areas and 615 in townships) from 11 kindergartens in Shunyi District were selected through stratified cluster random sampling. After fully paralyzing the ciliary muscle with 1% cyclopentolate, computerized refraction was performed to calculate the spherical equivalent (SE). myopia.summary: Myopia is a refractive anomaly, a global public health issue, mainly due to an increase in axial length of the eyeball. Myopia is increasing worldwide with the appearance of a "myopia global growing epidemic". …
myopia.abstract: Myopia is a refractive anomaly, a global public health issue, mainly due to an increase in axial length of the eyeball. Myopia is increasing worldwide with the appearance of a "myopia global growing epidemic". In children under 6 years old, 20 % have abnormalities, the most common of which are primarily refractive abnormalities, followed by strabismus and amblyopia. Myopia presents a major risk of complications, correlated with its severity, such as retinal detachment, retinal neovascularization, early cataracts and glaucoma. In children with high myopia, syndromic myopia must be explored. Early detection of myopia onset and progression is essential to myopia control strategies. The most promising treatments include outdoor activities, defocusing corrective lenses, defocusing contact lenses, orthokeratology and pharmacological treatments with low-dose atropine.

myopia.title: Overnight orthokeratology.
myopia.summary: Overnight orthokeratology lenses are approved in countries all over the world for the temporary reduction in myopia, and recently, one lens design has received regulatory approval for myopia control in Europe. …
myopia.abstract: Overnight orthokeratology lenses are approved in countries all over the world for the temporary reduction in myopia, and recently, one lens design has received regulatory approval for myopia control in Europe. The modern orthokeratology lens has a substantial history from its origins of attempting to flatten the corneal curvature with a spherical rigid contact lens to sophisticated gas permeable lenses, designed to reshape the cornea. These lenses are predominantly prescribed for children to slow myopia progression and limit axial elongation of the eye. This article reviews the peer-reviewed literature on the efficacy of orthokeratology for myopia control, sustainability after treatment is discontinued, and the safety concerns of overnight contact lens wear. Future avenues of research are discussed.

myopia.title: The epidemics of myopia: Aetiology and prevention.
myopia.summary: There is an epidemic of myopia in East and Southeast Asia, with the prevalence of myopia in young adults around 80-90%, and an accompanying high prevalence of high myopia in young adults (10-20%). This may foreshadow an increase in low vision and blindness due to pathological myopia. …
myopia.abstract: There is an epidemic of myopia in East and Southeast Asia, with the prevalence of myopia in young adults around 80-90%, and an accompanying high prevalence of high myopia in young adults (10-20%). This may foreshadow an increase in low vision and blindness due to pathological myopia. These two epidemics are linked, since the increasingly early onset of myopia, combined with high progression rates, naturally generates an epidemic of high myopia, with high prevalences of "acquired" high myopia appearing around the age of 11-13. The major risk factors identified are intensive education, and limited time outdoors. The localization of the epidemic appears to be due to the high educational pressures and limited time outdoors in the region, rather than to genetically elevated sensitivity to these factors. myopia.summary: The prevalence of myopia in children is increasing worldwide and is viewed as a major public health concern. This increase has driven interest in research into myopia prevention and control in children. …
myopia.abstract: The prevalence of myopia in children is increasing worldwide and is viewed as a major public health concern. This increase has driven interest in research into myopia prevention and control in children. Although there is still uncertainty in the risk factors underlying differences in myopia prevalence between ethnic groups, rates in children of East Asian descent are typically higher regardless of where they live. Mounting evidence also suggests that myopia prevalence in children increases with age. Earlier commencement and more rigorous education systems in these countries, resulting in more time spent on near-work activities and less time on outdoor activities, may be responsible for the earlier age of myopia onset. myopia.title: Efficacy in myopia control.
myopia.summary: There is rapidly expanding interest in interventions to slow myopia progression in children and teenagers, with the intent of reducing risk of myopia-associated complications later in life. …
myopia.abstract: There is rapidly expanding interest in interventions to slow myopia progression in children and teenagers, with the intent of reducing risk of myopia-associated complications later in life. Despite many publications dedicated to the topic, little attention has been devoted to understanding 'efficacy' in myopia control and its application. Treatment effect has been expressed in multiple ways, making comparison between therapies and prognosis for an individual patient difficult. Available efficacy data are generally limited to two to three years making long-term treatment effect uncertain. From an evidence-based perspective, efficacy projection should be conservative and not extend beyond that which has been empirically established. myopia.title: Defocus Incorporated Multiple Segments (DIMS) spectacle lenses slow myopia progression: a 2-year randomised clinical trial.
myopia.summary: Daily wear of the DIMS lens significantly retarded myopia progression and axial elongation in myopic children. Our results demonstrated simultaneous clear vision with constant myopic defocus can slow myopia progression.
myopia.abstract: AIM: To determine if 'Defocus Incorporated Multiple Segments' (DIMS) spectacle lenses slow childhood myopia progression. METHODS: A 2-year double-masked randomised controlled trial was carried out in 183 Chinese children aged 8-13 years, with myopia between -1.00 and -5.00 D and astigmatism ≤1.50 D. Children were randomly assigned to wear DIMS (n=93) or single vision (SV) spectacle lenses (n=90). DIMS lens incorporated multiple segments with myopic defocus of +3.50 D. Refractive error (cycloplegic autorefraction) and axial length were measured at 6month intervals. RESULTS: 160 children completed the study, n=79 in the DIMS group and n=81 in the SV group. myopia.summary: The 0.05%, 0.025%, and 0.01% atropine eye drops reduced myopia progression along a concentration-dependent response. All concentrations were well tolerated without an adverse effect on vision-related quality of life. …

Our study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of low-concentration atropine eye drops at 0.05%, 0.025%, and 0.01% compared with placebo over a 1-year period. myopia.abstract: Myopia is not a simple refractive error, but an eyesight-threatening disease. There is a high prevalence of myopia, 80% to 90%, in young adults in East Asia; myopia has become the leading cause of blindness in this area. As the myopic population increases globally, the severity of its impact is predicted. Approximately one fifth of the myopic population has high myopia (≥-6 diopters), which results in irreversible vision loss such as retinal detachment, choroidal neovascularization, cataracts, glaucoma, and macular atrophy. The increasing prevalence of school myopia in the past few decades may be a result of gene-environment interactions. However, earlier school myopia onset would accompany faster myopia progression and greater risk of high myopia later in life. myopia.summary: Myopia is a global problem that is increasing at an epidemic rate in the world. Although the refractive error can be corrected easily, myopes, particularly those with high myopia, are susceptible to potentially blinding eye diseases later in life. …
myopia.abstract: Myopia is a global problem that is increasing at an epidemic rate in the world. Although the refractive error can be corrected easily, myopes, particularly those with high myopia, are susceptible to potentially blinding eye diseases later in life. Despite a plethora of myopia research, the molecular/cellular mechanisms underlying the development of myopia are not well understood, preventing the search for the most effective pharmacological control. Consequently, several approaches to slowing down myopia progression in the actively growing eyes of children have been underway. So far, atropine, an anticholinergic blocking agent, has been most effective and is used by clinicians in off-label ways for myopia control. myopia.title: Preventing Myopia.
myopia.summary: Effective pharmacological and optical measures are now available to lessen the progression of myopia. The increasing prevalence of myopia should motivate pediatricians, parents, and schools to pay attention to risk factors such as close-up work and lack of daylight exposure, particularly in view of the increased use of digital media.
myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nearsightedness (myopia) has become more common around the world recently, mainly because of changes in visual, educational, and recreational behavior. The question arises how the risk of myopia and its progression can be reduced. This would lessen the prevalence and severity of myopia and also lower the risk of secondary diseases that impair visual acuity. METHODS: The PubMed/Medline database was selectively searched for pertinent literature. RESULTS: The risk of myopia is lowered by exposure to daylight and increased by activities performed at short visual distances (close-up work). A person with little exposure to daylight has a fivefold risk of developing myopia, which can rise as high as a 16-fold risk if that person also performs close-up work. myopia.summary: The school-based outdoor promotion program effectively reduced the myopia change in both nonmyopic and myopic children. Outdoor activities with strong sunlight exposure may not be necessary for myopia prevention. …

DESIGN: Multi-area, cluster-randomized intervention controlled trial. PARTICIPANTS: A total 693 grade 1 schoolchildren in 16 schools participated. Two hundred sixty-seven schoolchildren were in the intervention group and 426 were in the control group. METHODS: Initially, 24 schools were randomized into the intervention and control groups, but 5 and 3 schools in the intervention and control groups, respectively, withdrew before enrollment. A school-based Recess Outside Classroom Trial was implemented in the intervention group, in which schoolchildren were encouraged to go outdoors for up to 11 hours weekly. myopia.abstract: Myopia has been predicted to affect approximately 50% of the world's population based on trending myopia prevalence figures. Critical to minimizing the associated adverse visual consequences of complicating ocular pathologies are interventions to prevent or delay the onset of myopia, slow its progression, and to address the problem of mechanical instability of highly myopic eyes. Although treatment approaches are growing in number, evidence of treatment efficacy is variable. This article reviews research behind such interventions under four categories: optical, pharmacological, environmental (behavioral), and surgical. In summarizing the evidence of efficacy, results from randomized controlled trials have been given most weight, although such data are very limited for some treatments. Many studies have suggested that the frequently quoted myopia boom is related to changes in visual experiences during more demanding education and not due to changes in genetic factors. …
myopia.abstract: To avoid complications of high myopia the best solution would be to prevent myopia development from the very beginning. Many studies have suggested that the frequently quoted myopia boom is related to changes in visual experiences during more demanding education and not due to changes in genetic factors. To avoid myopia development it would therefore be best to carry out a better control of visual experience of children. In this article new approaches are described to record and improve visual habits in children, e.g. new sensors attached to the spectacle frames to document brightness, reading distance and reading duration, changes in text contrast polarity during reading, potential role of smartphones and some not yet fully explored orally applied substances to inhibit myopia.

myopia.title: Interventions to slow progression of myopia in children.
myopia.summary: Antimuscarinic topical medication is effective in slowing myopia progression in children. myopia.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nearsightedness (myopia) causes blurry vision when one is looking at distant objects. Interventions to slow the progression of myopia in children include multifocal spectacles, contact lenses, and pharmaceutical agents. OBJECTIVES: To assess the effects of interventions, including spectacles, contact lenses, and pharmaceutical agents in slowing myopia progression in children. SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL; Ovid MEDLINE; Embase.com; PubMed; the LILACS Database; and two trial registrations up to February 2018. A top up search was done in February 2019. SELECTION CRITERIA: We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs). We excluded studies when most participants were older than 18 years at baseline. myopia.title: Pharmacogenomic Approach to Antimyopia Drug Development: Pathways Lead the Way.
myopia.summary: Myopia is the most common eye disorder in the world which is caused by a mismatch between the optical power of the eye and its excessively long axial length. myopia.abstract: Myopia is the most common eye disorder in the world which is caused by a mismatch between the optical power of the eye and its excessively long axial length. Recent studies revealed that the regulation of the axial length of the eye occurs via a complex signaling cascade, which originates in the retina and propagates across all ocular tissues to the sclera. The complexity of this regulatory cascade has made it particularly difficult to develop effective antimyopia drugs. The current pharmacological treatment options for myopia are limited to atropine and 7-methylxanthine, which have either significant adverse effects or low efficacy. In this review, we focus on the recent advances in genome-wide studies of the signaling pathways underlying myopia development and discuss the potential of systems genetics and pharmacogenomic approaches for the development of antimyopia drugs.

myopia.title: Atropine for the treatment of childhood myopia: safety and efficacy of 0.5%, 0.1%, and 0.01% doses (Atropine for the Treatment of Myopia 2).
myopia.summary: Atropine 0.01% has minimal side effects compared with atropine at 0.1% and 0.5%, and retains comparable efficacy in controlling myopia progression.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: Our previous study, Atropine for the Treatment of Myopia 1 (ATOM1), showed that atropine 1% eyedrops were effective in controlling myopic progression but with visual side effects resulting from cycloplegia and mydriasis. The aim of this study was to compare efficacy and visual side effects of 3 lower doses of atropine: 0.5%, 0.1%, and 0.01%. DESIGN: Single-center, double-masked, randomized study. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 400 children aged 6-12 years with myopia of at least -2.0 diopters (D) and astigmatism of -1.50 D or less. INTERVENTION: Children were randomly assigned in a 2:2:1 ratio to 0.5%, 0.1%, and 0.01% atropine to be administered once nightly to both eyes for 2 years. Cycloplegic refraction, axial length, accommodation amplitude, pupil diameter, and visual acuity were noted at baseline, 2 weeks, and then every 4 months for 2 years. myopia.title: The complex interactions of retinal, optical and environmental factors in myopia aetiology.
myopia.summary: Myopia is the commonest ocular abnormality but as a research topic remains at the margins of mainstream ophthalmology. The concept that most myopes fall into the category of 'physiological myopia' undoubtedly contributes to this position. …
myopia.abstract: Myopia is the commonest ocular abnormality but as a research topic remains at the margins of mainstream ophthalmology. The concept that most myopes fall into the category of 'physiological myopia' undoubtedly contributes to this position. Yet detailed analysis of epidemiological data linking myopia with a range of ocular pathologies from glaucoma to retinal detachment demonstrates statistically significant disease association in the 0 to -6 D range of 'physiological myopia'. The calculated risks from myopia are comparable to those between hypertension, smoking and cardiovascular disease. In the case of myopic maculopathy and retinal detachment the risks are an order of magnitude greater. This finding highlights the potential benefits of interventions that can limit or prevent myopia progression. myopia.title: Time spent in outdoor activities in relation to myopia prevention and control: a meta-analysis and systematic review.
myopia.summary: Outdoor time is considered to reduce the risk of developing myopia. The purpose is to evaluate the evidence for association between time outdoors and (1) risk of onset of myopia (incident/prevalent myopia); (2) risk of a myopic shift in refractive error and c) risk of progression in myopes only. …
myopia.abstract: Outdoor time is considered to reduce the risk of developing myopia. The purpose is to evaluate the evidence for association between time outdoors and (1) risk of onset of myopia (incident/prevalent myopia); (2) risk of a myopic shift in refractive error and c) risk of progression in myopes only. A systematic review followed by a meta-analysis and a dose-response analysis of relevant evidence from literature was conducted. PubMed, EMBASE and the Cochrane Library were searched for relevant papers. Of the 51 articles with relevant data, 25 were included in the meta-analysis and dose-response analysis. Twenty-three of the 25 articles involved children. Risk ratio (RR) for binary variables and weighted mean difference (WMD) for continuous variables were conducted. myopia.title: Myopia Control 2020: Where are we and where are we heading?
myopia.summary: PURPOSE: This review arms practitioners with the evidence-based information they need to fully manage myopia. RECENT FINDINGS: The recent peer-reviewed literature is critically evaluated to provide a comprehensive analysis of the safety and efficacy of behavioural, optical and pharmaceutical myopia management. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: This review arms practitioners with the evidence-based information they need to fully manage myopia. RECENT FINDINGS: The recent peer-reviewed literature is critically evaluated to provide a comprehensive analysis of the safety and efficacy of behavioural, optical and pharmaceutical myopia management. Importantly, the paper addresses not only who to treat, but how to treat them, and when to stop or modify treatments. Finally, the paper discusses expectations for treatment and why slowing myopia by even 1 dioptre improves long term health outcomes. SUMMARY: The management of an individual child should be underpinned by the evidence-based literature and clinicians must stay alert to ongoing myopia research that will undoubtedly result in an evolution of the standard of care for the myopic and pre-myopic child.

myopia.title: Two-Year Clinical Trial of the Low-Concentration Atropine for Myopia Progression (LAMP) Study: Phase 2 Report.
myopia.summary: Over 2 years, the efficacy of 0.05% atropine observed was double that observed with 0.01% atropine, and it remained the optimal concentration among the studied atropine concentrations in slowing myopia progression.

DESIGN: Randomized, double-masked trial extended from the Low-Concentration Atropine for Myopia Progression (LAMP) Study. METHODS: Children in the placebo group (phase 1) were switched to receive 0.05% atropine from the beginning of the second-year follow-up, whereas those in the 0.05%, 0.025%, and 0.01% atropine groups continued with the same regimen. myopia.title: Commonly Held Beliefs About Myopia That Lack a Robust Evidence Base.
myopia.summary: There are many hypotheses proposed to explain phenomena in the myopia field. Caution should be exercised in adopting conjecture until a robust evidence base is provided in support.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To subject a number of commonly held beliefs or areas of confusion in the myopia field to scientific scrutiny. METHOD: A collection of statements about myopia are provided with references to demonstrate that a section of the research or clinical community supports the statement. These outcomes were classified as primary (refractive error and/or axial length), secondary (patient reported outcomes and treatment compliance), and exploratory (peripheral refraction, accommodative changes, ocular alignment, pupil size, outdoor activity/lighting levels, anterior and posterior segment imaging, and tissue biomechanics). The currently available instrumentation, which the literature has shown to best achieve the primary and secondary outcomes, was reviewed and critiqued. myopia.title: The Role of Orthokeratology in Myopia Control: A Review.
myopia.summary: The prevalence of myopia and high myopia has significantly increased worldwide and in the United States. The serious implications of these trends are being recognized. myopia.abstract: The prevalence of myopia and high myopia has significantly increased worldwide and in the United States. The serious implications of these trends are being recognized. Myopia is not just a minor inconvenience requiring vision correction with glasses or contact lenses, but a disease process creating significant risk of serious vision-threatening eye disease. Various methods of treatment for myopia and myopic progression have been prescribed and studied in effort to find one that is effective, safe, and that patients will be compliant with. Numerous peer-reviewed studies have shown orthokeratology (OrthoK) is effective in slowing myopic progression. This review article covers the development of OrthoK, its mechanism of action, its evolution, and refinement from a refractive option to its use as a mean of slowing myopic progression. myopia.title: Retardation of myopia in Orthokeratology (ROMIO) study: a 2-year randomized clinical trial.
myopia.summary: On average, subjects wearing ortho-k lenses had a slower increase in axial elongation by 43% compared with that of subjects wearing single-vision glasses. METHODS: A total of 102 eligible subjects, ranging in age from 6 to 10 years, with myopia between 0.50 and 4.00 diopters (D) and astigmatism not more than 1.25D, were randomly assigned to wear ortho-k lenses or single-vision glasses for a period of 2 years. myopia.summary: This network analysis indicates that a range of interventions can significantly reduce myopia progression when compared with single vision spectacle lenses or placebo. In terms of refraction, atropine, pirenzepine, and progressive addition spectacle lenses were effective. …

Elevating levels of myopia increase the risk of vision impairment, and therefore, high myopia has become one of the main causes of untreatable vision loss throughout the world due to its irreversible complications. At present, many options for slowing progression of myopia have already been proposed and evaluated such as progressive addition of executive bifocal spectacle lenses, peripheral defocusing lenses, overnight orthokeratology, pharmacological agents such as atropine eye drops, and multifocal soft contact lenses (MFSCLs). Highest frequencies have been found in East Asian urban populations (96.5%) but also a study in Europe shows that nearly half of the 25-29 year olds has myopia. With the increase in prevalence, high myopia, i.e. a spherical equivalent of -6 or more and an axial length of 26 mm or more is also on the rise. myopia.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Myopia refers to a refractive state of the eye that can predispose to visually significant ocular disease. The prevalence of myopia is increasing worldwide. Researchers internationally have been investigating methods to slow down its progression to prevent sight-threatening complications. In this article, we perform a review of the current literature discussing interventions for preventing pediatric myopic progression. RECENT FINDINGS: Various interventions, including lifestyle modification, optical methods, and pharmacologic approaches, have been proposed to help control myopic progression. OBJECTIVE: The aim of the study was to evaluate the additive effects of orthokeratology (OK) and 0.01% atropine ophthalmic solution for myopia in children. myopia.summary: Ortho-k treatment slows AL growth in the more myopic eye of anisometropic patients; should the contralateral eye develop myopia in the future, ortho-k is capable of slowing down AL growth in that eye as well.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the effect of orthokeratology (ortho-k) lens wear on axial length (AL) growth in juvenile myopic anisometropes. METHODS: This retrospective study consisted of two parts. In Part One, 25 anisometropic participants (mean age, 11.2 ± 1.9 years; 11 females and 14 males) were fitted with ortho-k lenses in the more myopic eye only, and the rate of AL growth was compared between the ortho-k lens wearing eye and the untreated contralateral eye over an average period of 23.1 ± 8.3 months. myopia.summary: Recent studies have confirmed that the prevalence of myopia has increased in most countries, that the increase must be due to environmental factors and that myopia is closely linked to the level of education. …

Extensive close-up work with short viewing distances, little outdoor activity and continuous exposure to low illumination are currently considered the major factors. myopia.summary: CLs were reported to be well accepted, consistent, and safe methods to address myopia regulation in children. Corneal refractive therapy (orthokeratology) is so far the method with the largest demonstrated efficacy in myopia regulation across different ethnic groups. …

The purpose of this report was to review our understanding of the rationale(s) and success of contact lenses (CLs) used to reduce myopia progression. METHODS: A review commenced by searching the PubMed database. myopia.summary: Pseudomyopia is one of many ocular and behavioral sequelae following TBI. By understanding the natural course and potential management options for post-traumatic pseudomyopia, the clinician will be better prepared to deal with these challenging cases. …

This apparent myopic shift disappears with cycloplegia, yet stubbornly reappears as soon as the pharmaceutical effect wears off. myopia.abstract: Myopia represents a failure of the normal process of emmetropization, which is essentially endogenous to the eye. Emmetropization involves defocus detection at the level of the amacrine and bipolar cells of the outer retina, diffusion of a signal or signals across the retinal pigment epithelium and choroid, and alteration of the scleral matrix, likely through modulation of proteoglycan synthesis. METHODS: Four hundred sixty-nine children enrolled in the Correction of Myopia Evaluation Trial (COMET; a multicenter, randomized, double-masked clinical trial evaluating the rate of progression of juvenile-onset myopia in children wearing progressive-addition versus single-vision lenses) were given 1 drop of proparacaine in each eye followed 1 minute later by 1 drop of 1% tropicamide and then a second drop of 1% tropicamide 4 to 6 minutes later. Five accommodative responses to 20/100 letters located at 4 m and 33 cm were obtained in each eye with an autorefractor, 20 minutes after the second drop. myopia.title: Binocular adaptation to near addition lenses in emmetropic adults.
myopia.summary: Near addition lenses are prescribed to pre-presbyopic individuals for treatment of binocular motor problems such as convergence excess and to control the progression of myopia. To date, no investigation has looked at the complete sequence of binocular motor responses during a period of near work with +2D lenses. …
myopia.abstract: Near addition lenses are prescribed to pre-presbyopic individuals for treatment of binocular motor problems such as convergence excess and to control the progression of myopia. To date, no investigation has looked at the complete sequence of binocular motor responses during a period of near work with +2D lenses. This investigation evaluated changes to accommodation and vergence responses when young adults sustained fixation at 33 cm with +2D addition lenses. In addition, the effect of the accommodative vergence cross-link (AV/A) on the magnitude and the completeness of binocular adaptation to these lenses were evaluated. The results showed that +2D lenses initiate an increase in exophoria and convergence driven accommodation. The degree of the initial induced phoria was dependant upon the magnitude of the AV/A ratio. myopia.title: Retinal detachment following phacoemulsification in highly myopic cataract patients.
myopia.summary: Retinal detachments following modern cataract surgery in high myopia are much less common than previously reported. We attribute this to small incision size, continued maintenance of the anterior chamber, posterior chamber IOL implantation, and lack of intraoperative complications.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess whether modern, small incision phacoemulsification techniques significantly reduce the retinal detachment (RD) risk in highly myopic patients who have visually significant cataracts. SETTING: University-associated ophthalmology practice. METHODS: This retrospective study included 80 eyes in 61 patients with preoperative myopia of 7.00 diopters (D) or more. Sixty-four eyes had an axial length of 25.0 mm or greater. All surgery was performed superiorly using a frown-shaped, self-sealing, scleral tunnel. The incision size ranged from 3.0 to 5.0 mm. Capsulorhexis was performed and then four-quadrant cracking phacoemulsification. The posterior capsule was routinely polished. A posterior chamber intraocular lens (IOL) was implanted in the capsular bag in all cases. myopia.title: Peripheral defocus does not necessarily affect central refractive development.
myopia.summary: There is extensive local compensation of imposed refractive errors in chickens. For the tested hole sizes, peripherally imposed defocus did not influence central refractive development. …
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: Recent experiments in monkeys suggest that deprivation, imposed only in the periphery of the visual field, can induce foveal myopia. This raises the hypothesis that peripheral refractive errors imposed by the spectacle lens correction could influence foveal refractive development also in humans. We have tested this hypothesis in chicks. METHODS: Chicks wore either full field spectacle lenses (+6.9 D/-7 D), or lenses with central holes of 4, 6, or 8mm diameter, for 4 days (n=6 for each group). Refractions were measured in the central visual field, and at -45 degrees (temporal) and +45 degrees (nasal), and axial lengths were measured by A-scan ultrasonography. myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To critically evaluate the following clinical wisdom regarding custom (wavefront-guided) laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) that subjects with better-than-average best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) before surgery have a greater risk of losing BCVA postoperatively than do subjects with worse-than-average BCVA before surgery. METHODS: High contrast BCVA was measured once before and 3 months after custom LASIK in one eye of 79 subjects. Preoperative spherical equivalent refractive error ranged between -1.00 and -10.38 D. The sample was divided into one of two subsamples: eyes that had better-than-average preoperative BCVA (<-0.11 logMAR) and eyes that had average or worse-than-average preoperative BCVA (≥-0.11 logMAR). myopia.title: A study of aniseikonia and Knapp's law using a projection space eikonometer.
myopia.summary: As a geometric optics theory, Knapp's Law stands on its own merits. However, in clinical practice, reduction in retinal element density in high myopia limits its applicability. Such patients often do have significant aniseikonia which can produce ocular referable complaints and/or interfere with binocular vision.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: Knapp's Law, which states that anisometropias due to varying abnormal axial lengths between eyes would not result in inequality in relative retinal image size, provided the correcting spectacle lens was placed at the far point of the eye, has been shown to fall short in clinical practice in several studies using "direct comparison eikonometry". To test these findings using space eikonometry and to further elucidate this Law's clinical applicability, the following study was conducted. METHODS: Thirteen patients with suspected axial anisometropia of at least 4 Diopters were identified, selected and examined. Cycloplegic refraction, A-scan ultrasonic ocular biometry and Essilor Projection Space Eikonometry were performed. myopia.title: Pharmacotherapy of photorefractive keratectomy.
myopia.summary: In general, high-volume PRK surgeons use topical steroids, NSAIDs, and a soft contact lens in the immediate postoperative period, although they are uncertain about the long-term effectiveness of NSAIDs in controlling regression and haze.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare the pharmacotherapeutic practices of high-volume photorefractive keratectomy (PRK) surgeons with suggested practices gleaned from the current literature. SETTING: York Finch Eye Associates, Toronto, Canada. METHODS: Seventy-five ophthalmic surgeons believed by the authors to do a high-volume of PRKs were surveyed over the summer of 1994 about their pharmacotherapeutic practices. The results were compared with suggested practices extracted from a review of the current literature. RESULTS: Relatively consistent approaches to the management of post-PRK pain and prevention of acute post-PRK subepithelial infiltrative keratitis were reported. The administration of topical steroids after PRK was almost universally employed. myopia.title: Effect of myopia on visual acuity measured with laser interference fringes.
myopia.summary: The aim was to determine how visual acuity is affected by myopia when optical factors of the eye are controlled. Grating acuity was measured with interference fringes to avoid the effects of aberrations, and ocular biometry was used to compensate for differences in retinal image size among subjects. …
myopia.abstract: The aim was to determine how visual acuity is affected by myopia when optical factors of the eye are controlled. Grating acuity was measured with interference fringes to avoid the effects of aberrations, and ocular biometry was used to compensate for differences in retinal image size among subjects. Distance spectacle refractions ranged from +2.25 to -14.75 D. The retinal magnification factor (RMF) in mm/deg was computed for each eye from the distance refraction, central corneal power and ultrasound biometry. A forced-choice orientation discrimination method was used to measure acuity for high-contrast 543 nm laser interference fringes in three retinal locations: the fovea, and at 4 deg and 10 deg eccentricity in the temporal retina. Acuity, expressed in c/deg and adjusted for spectacle magnification, was not significantly correlated with refraction at any of the three retinal locations.

myopia.title: Effects of retinal dopamine depletion on the growth of the fish eye.
myopia.summary: We investigated the suitability of fishes as animal models to study the involvement of the retinal dopaminergic system in the visually guided control of eye growth (emmetropization). …
myopia.abstract: We investigated the suitability of fishes as animal models to study the involvement of the retinal dopaminergic system in the visually guided control of eye growth (emmetropization). Advantages of such a model system are (i) that all dopaminergic cells in the retina can be destroyed without apparent damage to other neurons, (ii) simple optical design and short depth of field of the eye, and (iii) continuous growth throughout life. Depleting the retina of dopamine in Aequidens pulcher (Cichlidae) had no apparent effect on refractive state, since size and focal length of the eye were reduced by the same amount. Furthermore, imposed defocus was compensated at a normal rate in spite of the absence of retinal dopamine. myopia.title: Phakic intraocular lens correction of high ametropia in children with neurobehavioral disorders.
myopia.summary: Phakic IOL implantation improves visual function substantially in neurobehaviorally impaired children who have high ametropia and difficulties wearing glasses.
myopia.abstract: PURPOSE: A subset of children with high ametropia and neurobehavioral disorders have chronic difficulties with spectacle or contact lens wear. We report the results of refractive surgery in a series of these children treated using bilateral or unilateral phakic intraocular lenses (IOLs) for ametropia >10 D. METHODS: Clinical course and outcome data were collated prospectively in a group of 12 children (mean age, 10.1 years; range, 4-17 years) with neurobehavioral disorders exacerbated by poor compliance with spectacles. Myopia in 18 eyes ranged from -10.0 to -22.75 D (mean, -15.2 D) and in 2 hyperopic eyes from +10.25 to +10.75 (mean, +10.5 D). Goal refraction was approximately 0 to +1 D. Correction was achieved by implantation of an iris-enclaved phakic IOL under general anesthesia. Mean follow-up was 9.1 months (range, 3-15 months). METHODS: The expression of the brain-derived neurotrophic factor, neurotrophin-3, sonic hedgehog, nerve growth factor, Six-3 and the Lh-2 group of genes in the transcriptional level after experimentally induced myopia (form-deprivation by goggles and by hyperopic defocus using negative spectacle lenses) were evaluated by semiquantitative reverse transcriptional polymerase chain reaction and Northern blot analysis. myopia.title: Night myopia and driving.
myopia.summary: Current knowledge of the refractive shifts (twilight myopia, night myopia, dark focus) that occur as the luminance is progressively lowered from photopic levels is reviewed. In complete darkness, myopic changes of the order of 1 dioptre are typical in young adult subjects. These gradually diminish as presbyopia is approached. …
myopia.abstract: Current knowledge of the refractive shifts (twilight myopia, night myopia, dark focus) that occur as the luminance is progressively lowered from photopic levels is reviewed. In complete darkness, myopic changes of the order of 1 dioptre are typical in young adult subjects. These gradually diminish as presbyopia is approached. The possible role of these refractive changes in causing visual difficulties for young drivers on the road at night is considered. It is concluded that high mesopic levels (about 1 cd/m2) of road luminance produced by street and vehicle lighting are normally too great to allow significant refractive shifts to occur, although acuity will be reduced due to light-dependent neural changes.
