lens.summary: We compared a rapid fifth-generation (5G) objectiveFIELD Analyser® (OFA®) test with two fourth-generation (4G) 8 min tests in the assessment of glaucoma. lens.abstract: We compared a rapid fifth-generation (5G) objectiveFIELD Analyser® (OFA®) test with two fourth-generation (4G) 8 min tests in the assessment of glaucoma. We assessed the relative diagnostic power of these three OFA tests, namely two high-resolution 4G tests (wide-field OFA30 and macular OFA15), and a new 5G 90 s test (wide-field OFA30-20). Glaucomatous eyes were classified into mild, moderate, and severe based upon the Matrix 24-2 perimetry Mean Defect (MD). We tested 37 glaucoma patients (11 females) aged 70.5 ± 9.19 years. Their average Matrix MD was -7.71 ± 6.35 dB. Age-matched normal controls were acquired for the 4G and 5G tests. lens.summary: Background/Objectives: The human telomerase reverse transcriptase (hTERT) maintains mitochondrial DNA, modulates the release of reactive oxygen species, and contributes to axonal regeneration. lens.abstract: Background/Objectives: The human telomerase reverse transcriptase (hTERT) maintains mitochondrial DNA, modulates the release of reactive oxygen species, and contributes to axonal regeneration. Previous work reported that hTERT levels in the tear film may reflect stress and loss of homeostasis in dry eyes. This was accompanied by morphological changes in corneal nerves. In episodic migraines, oxidative stress, imbalance in antioxidant defense, and mitochondrial dysfunction play a major role in the pathogenesis, and changes in corneal nerves have been reported to occur. Against this, the current study primarily aimed to investigate tear film hTERT levels in individuals with episodic migraine. A secondary aim was to assess the relationship between tear film hTERT levels and morphological changes in corneal nerves. lens.summary: Short-term mobile e-sports are associated with microvascular modulations and cone morphological alterations in the posterior segment following high-intensity visual workload. …
lens.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To observe the hemodynamic and morphological changes in the macular retinochoroidal microcirculation and cone photoreceptor following short-term mobile e-sports. METHODS: This observational study enrolled 35 healthy young participants. After a standardized 15-minute resting period, participants played a 15-minute mobile game (Honor of Kings). Before and after the game, swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT) was used to measure subfoveal choroidal thickness (SFCT), and swept-source optical coherence tomography angiography (SS-OCTA) was used to measure foveal choroidal vascular volume (CVV). Adaptive optics scanning laser ophthalmoscopy (AO-SLO) was utilized to track morphological parameter changes in cone photoreceptors. lens.title: Association between reading-related oculomotor performance and selective and sustained visual attention in school-aged children.
lens.summary: Selective and sustained visual attention and oculomotor performance improved with age. The findings suggest a relationship between visual attention and oculomotor control, although the association between attention difficulties and DEM dysfunction was not statistically significant.
lens.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the association between eye movements and selective and sustained visual attention in children aged 6-13 years using the Developmental Eye Movement (DEM) test and a visual cancellation task. METHODS: This study included 217 children aged 6-13 years. Reading-related oculomotor performance was assessed using the Developmental Eye Movement (DEM) test. Selective and sustained visual attention was assessed using the 2/3 signal cancellation test. Results were analyzed by age and sex, and the association between attentional performance and DEM test classification was examined. RESULTS: Performance on the cancellation task was significantly better in adolescents than in younger school-aged children, with significant associations between age and attentional outcomes. lens.title: Automating systematic reviews in ophthalmology with the use of large language model deep research tools.
lens.summary: GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 showed low data reporting error rates in evidence synthesis; however, incomplete literature coverage, bibliography management issues and poor adherence to reporting guidelines mandate human oversight, especially in study selection and quality appraisal.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the performance of large language model (LLM) 'Deep Research' agentic systems for writing systematic reviews (SRs) in ophthalmology. METHODS: Structured prompts were submitted in September 2026 to Deep Research tools powered by GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 to produce SRs on the topics of 50 human-authored SRs published between May and August 2026 in ophthalmology journals (2025 Journal Impact Factor ≥ 3). Main outcomes included literature coverage (recall and precision against the studies included in the human-made SRs on the same topics), data extraction accuracy (discrepant numerical findings against cited sources), percentage of valid references and PRISMA adherence. lens.title: Assessment of Visual Quality Changes as a Result of Spectacle Misalignment.
lens.summary: Background: A substantial proportion of presbyopic patients experience visual symptoms or fail to adapt to progressive addition lenses (PALs), and lens tilt caused by suboptimal frame fitting has been suggested as one of the possible contributing factors. …
lens.abstract: Background: A substantial proportion of presbyopic patients experience visual symptoms or fail to adapt to progressive addition lenses (PALs), and lens tilt caused by suboptimal frame fitting has been suggested as one of the possible contributing factors. The aim of this theoretical study was to quantify the sensitivity of retinal image quality, wavefront aberrations and model-predicted monocular visual acuity to controlled horizontal and vertical misalignment (tilt) of single-vision (SV) spectacle lenses across a range of spherical refractive powers and viewing directions. No clinical, comfort or adaptation outcome was measured. lens.title: Occupational Radiation Effects on Ocular Structures and Visual Function: A Comprehensive Review.
lens.summary: Occupational radiation exposure can affect ocular health across medical, nuclear, aviation, outdoor, welding, and other specialized workplace settings. This narrative review is primarily focused on occupational ocular radiation injury and occupational eye protection. …
lens.abstract: Occupational radiation exposure can affect ocular health across medical, nuclear, aviation, outdoor, welding, and other specialized workplace settings. This narrative review is primarily focused on occupational ocular radiation injury and occupational eye protection. It prioritizes human occupational evidence on ionizing radiation and occupationally relevant non-ionizing optical hazards, particularly solar ultraviolet exposure, welding, and lasers, while using experimental or non-occupational evidence only when needed to clarify mechanisms or areas of uncertainty. Evidence is strongest for an association between occupational ionizing radiation and crystalline lens opacity or cataract, whereas evidence for routine occupational effects on the retina, optic nerve, or macula is substantially weaker. lens.title: Oculomotor Behavior in Youth Ice Hockey Skaters and Goaltenders During Sport-Specific Tasks.
lens.summary: Ice hockey requires rapid visual processing and continuous oculomotor adjustments that may vary according to player role and task demands. This study aimed to characterize the oculomotor behavior of ice hockey skaters and goaltenders during sport-specific tasks performed under real on-ice conditions and to assess variations across repeate …
lens.abstract: Ice hockey requires rapid visual processing and continuous oculomotor adjustments that may vary according to player role and task demands. This study aimed to characterize the oculomotor behavior of ice hockey skaters and goaltenders during sport-specific tasks performed under real on-ice conditions and to assess variations across repeated trials or consecutive shots. Twenty-seven players (16 skaters and 11 goaltenders) underwent a comprehensive optometric examination before testing with a wearable Neon Eye Tracker (Pupil Labs, 200 Hz). Skaters completed two repetitions of a circuit comprising zigzag puck handling, dibbling, and shooting, whereas goaltenders faced nine consecutive shots on goal. lens.title: Emmetropic and myopic retinal reconstruction from peripheral ocular biometry.
lens.summary: To investigate differences in retinal shape between emmetropic and myopic eyes, peripheral biometry measurements were obtained for 54 young adult eyes using partial coherence interferometry. An ellipsoid model was fitted to each retina to determine the axial and transverse semiaxes, radii of curvature, asphericities, and decentrations. …
lens.abstract: To investigate differences in retinal shape between emmetropic and myopic eyes, peripheral biometry measurements were obtained for 54 young adult eyes using partial coherence interferometry. An ellipsoid model was fitted to each retina to determine the axial and transverse semiaxes, radii of curvature, asphericities, and decentrations. Linear mixed-effects models were applied to evaluate significance, correlations, and trends. The retinal asphericities reduced with increasing myopia and axial length (p < 0.05), while the axial semiaxis increased (p < 0.05). Emmetropic retinas exhibited oblate shapes (Q x , Q y  > 0), whereas myopic retinas were less oblate (p < 0.05). Finally, a significant asymmetry between horizontal and vertical meridians (p < 0.05) was found in both groups.

lens.title: Practice-Level Implementation of 0.4% Pilocarpine for Presbyopia: A Multicenter, Single-Arm Pilot Study of Key Practice Outcomes.
lens.summary: When implemented within a structured prescribing pathway, pilo 0.4% was not associated with reductions in optical purchasing or ancillary testing utilization during the study period, suggesting feasibility of integration into routine optometric practice. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Despite the growing availability of pharmacologic options for presbyopia management, the practice-level implications of prescribing miotic agents within an optometric setting remain largely unexplored. Practitioners have expressed concern that prescribing these agents might reduce the use or purchase of optical corrective devices, or otherwise disrupt established revenue streams. The Presbyopia Pathway Implementation Pilot was undertaken to address these concerns using real-world, practice-based data. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This multicenter, single-arm, open-label pilot study assessed the impact of pilocarpine hydrochloride ophthalmic solution 0.4% (pilo 0.4%; Qlosi, Orasis Pharmaceuticals) on key performance indicators (KPIs) across seven optometric practice sites within a large, multicenter organization. lens.title: Association between daily near-vision duration and visual symptom burden among university staff: a cross-sectional study.
lens.summary: Longer daily near-vision duration was associated with greater visual symptom burden, and higher CISS score was associated with self-reported work impact. Assessing visual symptoms alongside near-work duration may help occupational health services identify staff who could benefit from eye examination and workplace assessment.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: University staff routinely perform prolonged near-viewing tasks that may contribute to visual symptoms and work-related difficulties. We examined the associations of daily near-vision duration with Convergence Insufficiency Symptom Survey (CISS) score and of near-vision duration and CISS score with self-reported work impact. METHODS: This cross-sectional survey included 255 university staff members. Daily near-vision duration was analyzed per 2 h/day. Linear regression estimated adjusted mean differences in continuous CISS score, and modified Poisson regression estimated prevalence ratios (PRs) for CISS score ≥21 and self-reported work impact. lens.title: Visual field performance of the novel DIMS TED spectacle lens compared with DIMS and single-vision spectacle lenses.
lens.summary: The DIMS TED spectacle lens was associated with no clinically meaningful reduction in visual field sensitivity within the central 30° compared with DIMS and SV spectacle lenses in myopic children. This finding supports the visual tolerability of this intensified defocus design for childhood myopia management. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the visual field performance of DIMS TED spectacle lens, an enhanced Defocus Incorporated Multiple Segments (DIMS) spectacle lens design featuring more defocus segments closer to the geometric center, higher defocus power and extended defocus treatment zone, compared with DIMS and single vision (SV) spectacle lenses. METHODS: Children aged 9 to 14 years with cycloplegic spherical equivalent refractive error (SER) ranged from -1.00 to -6.00D were recruited. Visual field performance was assessed using an automated static perimeter (Zeiss, Humphrey Visual Field HFA 750i) with SITA Fast 30-2 protocol. A Goldmann size III (0.43o) green flashing stimulus of varying luminance levels was presented at 76 random test points within 30o visual field. lens.title: Effect of Pupillary Dilation on Image Gradeability and Diagnostic Performance in AI-Based Diabetic Retinopathy Detection Among Older Adults - A Clinical Evaluation.
lens.summary: Our findings indicate that pupillary dilation significantly improved retinal image gradeability and reduced repeated imaging in older adults. Although diagnostic accuracy metrics remained stable, the higher proportion of gradable images enabled more patients to benefit from AI-assisted DR detection. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Artificial intelligence (AI) has demonstrated significant potential in detecting diabetic retinopathy (DR) from retinal images. However, image acquisition in older adults is often affected by constricted pupils and media opacity. This study evaluated the effect of pupillary dilation on retinal image gradeability and diagnostic yield in AI-assisted DR detection among older adults. METHODS: In this prospective study, adults aged ≥65 years were recruited from a tertiary eye hospital in India. Retinal images were captured using a clinically validated AI-integrated fundus camera (Optain Resolve OPTFC01, Optain Health, Melbourne, Australia) before and after pupillary dilation. lens.title: Achieving natural eye and lens interaction based eyeglasses optical fit through a parametric customization approach.
lens.summary: Eyeglasses are widely used to correct refractive errors, but optical fit evaluation usually emphasizes lens design alone and mainly assumes uniform use of the lens aperture. This can increase design complexity and cost while overlooking how the eye interacts with the lens during everyday wear. …
lens.abstract: Eyeglasses are widely used to correct refractive errors, but optical fit evaluation usually emphasizes lens design alone and mainly assumes uniform use of the lens aperture. This can increase design complexity and cost while overlooking how the eye interacts with the lens during everyday wear. Here we show that favorable eyeglasses optical fit can be achieved through head-anthropometry-based parametric frame customization within the context of natural eye and lens interaction. We combined parametric frame design with mathematical lens modeling and evaluated both myopia and presbyopia groups. The results show that appropriate frame customization can maintain rational control of oblique aberrations for spherical and basic aspheric lenses without relying on high-order lens terms. lens.title: Initial Perceptions of Visual Quality and User Satisfaction with Verofilcon a Spherical Daily Disposable Silicone Hydrogel Contact Lens in First-Time Adolescent Contact Lens Wearers: A Pilot Study.
lens.summary: Our preliminary findings indicate that adolescent neophyte CL users have high rates of satisfaction in vision, comfort, appearance, and handling with daily verofilcon A CLs. We found that participants did not respond differently based on their sex and refractive error.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: The purpose of our study was to assess the initial impressions of comfort, vision, and lens-associated quality of life (QoL) in adolescent neophyte CL wearers. We also determined if participants responded differently based on their sex and refractive error. METHODS: This was a prospective, non-comparative, single-arm pilot study. A total of 28 new CL wearing adolescents aged 13 to <18 years completed the study. There were 3 total visits: baseline, 1-week, and a 3-week follow-up. At baseline, participants were surveyed on initial impression of lens comfort and trained on CL handling. After 3 weeks, participants were surveyed using a non-validated questionnaire on comfort, vision, and performance during daily activities while wearing the lens. lens.title: Inflammatory lesions in punctate inner choroidopathy and posterior globe curvature: a widefield OCT analysis.
lens.summary: PIC preferentially occurs in highly myopic eyes with posterior staphyloma. Although global curvature metrics were primarily related to axial elongation rather than PIC status, inflammatory lesions showed a non-random spatial distribution, clustering near-but not directly over-the steepest posterior curvatures. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate how inflammatory lesion distribution in punctate inner choroidopathy (PIC) relates to posterior globe morphology using widefield optical coherence tomography (OCT). METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, 62 eyes (47 with PIC and 15 fellow non-PIC eyes) from 32 patients underwent widefield swept-source OCT. Structural features, including axial length (AL), Gaussian curvature, and curvature gradient metrics, were compared between PIC and non-PIC eyes using mixed-effects models. lens.title: Cannabis Impairment and Intrinsically Photosensitive Retinal Ganglion Cells.
lens.summary: PURPOSE: Technologies to better determine impairment from cannabis use are essential. Understanding the functional losses that can occur with any use, medical or adult recreational use, will better assure the safety of individuals as well as the public. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Technologies to better determine impairment from cannabis use are essential. Understanding the functional losses that can occur with any use, medical or adult recreational use, will better assure the safety of individuals as well as the public. This study evaluated the Frequency Doubling Technology 710 (FDT710) tabletop field test as a screening tool for detecting retinal dysfunction associated with inhaled cannabis use. Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the psychoactive component of cannabis, has been shown to impair dopaminergic dependent intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cell (ipRGC) functioning. lens.title: Arabic reading performance: orthographic challenges, standardization barriers, and insights from emerging empirical research.
lens.summary: Arabic orthography amplifies the visual processing load experienced by individuals with reading difficulties due to its cursive structure, curved letterforms, and extensive use of diacritical marks. …
lens.abstract: Arabic orthography amplifies the visual processing load experienced by individuals with reading difficulties due to its cursive structure, curved letterforms, and extensive use of diacritical marks. This review highlights the growing body of research on Arabic reading performance, facilitated by the development of a standardised Arabic reading chart that has enabled systematic investigation of the visual, linguistic, and cognitive factors influencing readability. Although several aspects of Arabic reading resemble patterns observed in Latin-based languages, the distinctive orthographic complexity of Arabic underscores the need for continued empirical work to refine experimental methods, establish functional benchmarks, and advance a comprehensive model of Arabic reading capable of informing both clinical assessment and educational practice. lens.title: Depressive symptoms and Predictors Among Adult Myopic Patients Attending a Tertiary Eye Care Center in Northwest Ethiopia: Institution-Based Cross-Sectional Study.
lens.summary: Relatively higher magnitudes of depressive symptoms were observed among adult myopic patients. Factors such as high myopia, severe visual impairment, advanced age, and no formal education were significantly associated with depressive symptoms. …
lens.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Depression is a common comorbidity among individuals with visual impairment, including those with myopia. Functional limitations, reduced quality of life, and psychosocial challenges associated with vision loss may increase the risk of depressive symptoms. OBJECTIVES: To assess the prevalence of depressive symptoms and associated factors among adult myopic patients attending a tertiary eye care center in northwestern Ethiopia. METHODS: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 418 adult myopic patients from June 10 to September 10, 2024. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the Patient Health Questionnaire-9. lens.title: Ocular Morbidity and Associated Factors Among Garo Adults in Madhupur, Bangladesh.
lens.summary: Background Indigenous populations may experience substantial barriers to accessing eye care services, yet evidence on ocular morbidity among the Garo community in Bangladesh remains limited. This study assessed the burden and factors associated with ocular morbidity among Garo adults in Madhupur, Tangail. …
lens.abstract: Background Indigenous populations may experience substantial barriers to accessing eye care services, yet evidence on ocular morbidity among the Garo community in Bangladesh remains limited. This study assessed the burden and factors associated with ocular morbidity among Garo adults in Madhupur, Tangail. Methods A community-based cross-sectional study of 111 Garo adults aged 18 and older was conducted in Pirgacha, Madhupur, Tangail, from June 2024 to July 2025. Participants received structured interviews and ocular assessments, including visual acuity (VA), refraction, and anterior- and posterior segment examinations. lens.summary: Photoreceptor synapses rely on mitochondria, synaptic ribbons, and vesicles, yet how these elements integrate into functional units remains unclear. lens.abstract: Photoreceptor synapses rely on mitochondria, synaptic ribbons, and vesicles, yet how these elements integrate into functional units remains unclear. Here we show, using focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) and electrophysiology, that they form synaptic mitochondrion-ribbon-vesicle complexes (sMRVcs) with fundamentally different architectures in rods and cones. Rod spherules exhibit a strict 1:1 pairing of a single megamitochondrion with one ribbon, sustaining continuous glutamate release in darkness, whereas cone pedicles contain multiple distributed sMRVcs. Disrupting the mitochondrial anchor protein syntaphilin shifts this ratio to 2:1 in rods, with additional mitochondria recruited near the ribbon, and enhances synaptic transmission. lens.title: Relationship Between Chromatic Sensitivity and Retinal Structure in Early Glaucoma.
lens.summary: Glaucoma patients show reduced chromatic sensitivity in every stage of severity. Results suggest that changes in both outer and inner retinal layers influence chromatic sensitivity. The outer retinal layer thickness is more strongly associated with color thresholds across all disease severity stages in glaucoma.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the correlations between retinal structure parameters and chromatic sensitivity in controls and people with various stages of primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG) and ocular hypertension (OHT). A secondary aim was to assess the diagnostic and predictive accuracy of red/green (RG) and yellow/blue (YB) chromatic thresholds in identifying early glaucomatous alterations. METHODS: One hundred sixty-nine participants were recruited (n = 25 OHT, n = 33 early, n = 11 moderate, n = 11 severe POAG, and n = 89 controls) from the glaucoma clinic at St. Thomas's Hospital. Chromatic sensitivity was measured with the Color Assessment and Diagnostics (CAD) test. lens.title: Spatio-Temporal Choriocapillaris Flow Deficits Are Associated With Outer Retinal Degeneration and Visual Function in Geographic Atrophy.
lens.summary: CC flow deficits are associated with local GA progression, especially observed direct conversion, and with visual decline in foveal-sparing eyes. FD% added limited predictive value beyond structural biomarkers but remained an independent vascular correlate of conversion risk that may complement OCT-based risk stratification.

lens.summary: Macular OCT provided structural information beyond VA and showed similar discrimination to optic-nerve OCT. Longitudinal summaries offered no clear gain over baseline OCT, while GCL++ alone showed strong discrimination.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate whether macular optical coherence tomography (OCT) distinguishes eyes with versus without recorded magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-defined eye-level optic pathway glioma (OPG) status in neurofibromatosis type 1, and whether longitudinal OCT, visual/clinical variables, optic-nerve, or single-feature OCT add value. Six primary feature sets compared baseline and longitudinal macular OCT, with and without clinical/visual variables, plus clinical/visual variables alone and visual acuity (VA) alone. lens.title: Multifocal toric contact lenses improve low-contrast reading performance in presbyopes with moderate astigmatism.
lens.summary: The functional benefits with the contact lenses tested depend on both the magnitude of astigmatism and the visual task assessed. Although toric correction improved distance VA, an additional benefit of multifocal toric over multifocal spherical correction was observed for low-contrast reading speed in presbyopes with moderate astigmatism. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the effects of multifocal toric contact lens correction on visual acuity (VA), functional reading performance, oculomotor behaviour and subjective visual outcomes in presbyopic contact lens wearers with low to moderate myopic astigmatism. ΜETHODS: Twenty-four presbyopic volunteers (50 ± 3 years) classified into low (0.75 DC, N = 15) or moderate (1.25 DC, N = 9) lens-cylinder groups were fitted in a masked crossover design, with three monthly silicone hydrogel contact lens types: toric (T, comfilcon A), multifocal-spherical (MS, lotrafilcon B) and multifocal toric (MT, asmofilcon A). Binocular VA was measured at far, intermediate and near distances. Silent reading performance was assessed using infrared eye tracking during reading of standardised passages presented at high and low contrast. lens.title: Uncovering the genetic architecture of optic nerve integrity estimates through genome-wide association study meta-analyses.
lens.summary: BACKGROUND: The peripapillary retinal nerve fibre layer (pRNFL) thickness and Bruch's membrane opening-minimum rim width (BMO-MRW) are structural biomarkers for glaucoma. We conducted large-scale multi-cohort genome-wide association meta-analyses of global and sectoral pRNFL thickness and BMO-MRW to disentangle their genetic architecture. …
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: The peripapillary retinal nerve fibre layer (pRNFL) thickness and Bruch's membrane opening-minimum rim width (BMO-MRW) are structural biomarkers for glaucoma. We conducted large-scale multi-cohort genome-wide association meta-analyses of global and sectoral pRNFL thickness and BMO-MRW to disentangle their genetic architecture. METHODS: We included up to 25,942 and 12,080 participants for global and sectoral pRNFL thickness and BMO-MRW, respectively, from the International Glaucoma Genetics Consortium. Conditional analysis was used to identify loci with association evidence beyond intraocular pressure (IOP). lens.title: Refractive status and visual function in patients with pre-presbyopia and presbyopia wearing monofocal soft contact lenses without glasses in daily life.
lens.summary: Patients with presbyopia wearing monofocal CLs showed significant declines in NVA and DVA in their 50s, with trends toward undercorrection, possibly to compensate for near visual impairment. Age, sex, and pupillary dynamics should be considered when optimising refractive correction.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate the refractive status and visual function of patients with pre-presbyopia and presbyopia using monofocal soft contact lenses (CLs) without glasses in daily life. STUDY DESIGN: Cross-sectional observational study METHODS: We included 102 participants wearing monofocal soft CLs without glasses. lens.title: Prevalence and Associations of Depressive and Anxiety Symptoms in Age Related Macular Degeneration and Other Macular Diseases.
lens.summary: Depressive and anxiety symptoms among older adults with macular disease are both associated with loneliness, high falls concern and poor sleep quality. The multifactorial nature of mental health outcomes highlights the need for holistic, patient-centred care that incorporates mental health screening and appropriate referral pathways.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Older people with visual impairments are at risk of poor mental health and often do not seek mental health support. This study investigated the prevalence and associations of depression and anxiety in people with age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and other macular diseases. METHODS: A cross-sectional survey was conducted among people with AMD and other macular diseases in Australia. Key outcomes of depression and anxiety were measured using the 15-item Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS-15) and the 7-item Generalised Anxiety Disorder scale (GAD-7). Associations between symptoms of depression and anxiety and clinical, demographic and psychosocial variables were explored in multivariable logistic regression analyses, with multiple imputations for missing data. lens.title: Integrative Multi-Omics in Glaucoma: Defining Mechanistic Axes and Enabling Precision Management.
lens.summary: Glaucoma is increasingly recognized not as a uniform pressure-defined optic neuropathy, but rather as a heterogeneous neurodegenerative disorder driven by interacting genetic, metabolic, mechanical, vascular, inflammatory, and environmental factors. …
lens.abstract: Glaucoma is increasingly recognized not as a uniform pressure-defined optic neuropathy, but rather as a heterogeneous neurodegenerative disorder driven by interacting genetic, metabolic, mechanical, vascular, inflammatory, and environmental factors. Although genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics have each yielded important insights, no single omics layer can fully capture the multilevel architecture underlying differences in disease susceptibility, progression, and treatment response. Multi-omics therefore offers a more integrated framework for linking inherited risk, gene regulation, cellular states, protein activity, metabolic vulnerability, and imaging phenotypes to clinically relevant outcomes. This review summarizes recent advances in multi-omics research in glaucoma, spanning genomics, epigenomics and transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and lipidomics, micro

lens.title: Spatial Localization With Low Vision: Sensory Integration From Patient Perspectives.
lens.summary: LV individuals perceived auditory localization as easier than visual yet predominantly reported vision as their primary sense. Integration benefit was reduced in LV, possibly due to an over-reliance on vision.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Everyday spatial localization depends on both vision and hearing. We examine how low vision (LV) affects the perceived contributions of vision and hearing in everyday spatial localization using the Dual Sensory Spatial Localization Questionnaire (DS-SLQ). METHODS: Seventy-five participants with normal hearing (37 with normal vision [NV], and 38 with LV) completed a 62-item DS-SLQ, rating overall, vision-only, and hearing-only difficulty for spatial localization and reporting primary sense for each task. Rasch analysis estimated item measures (perceived task difficulty), person measures (perceived ability), and functional reserves (difference between each pair of item and person measure). RESULTS: NV participants rated the tasks as easier with vision-only than hearing-only, whereas the opposite was observed in the LV group. Overall perceived ability was only associated with visio

lens.title: Time at the curb, not the rate of head scanning, distinguishes street crossing in virtual reality with severe-to-profound visual impairment.
lens.summary: Severe-to-profound visual impairment was associated with longer and more variable time at the curb, without a significant increase in cumulative head scanning, although the increase in head scanning with complexity during walking was attenuated. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: We tested whether people with severe-to-profound visual impairment compensate at street crossings with more head scanning and/or more time at the curb. METHODS: Ten normally sighted controls, tested with normal vision and with Bangerter filters simulating severe-to-profound visual impairment (approximately 20/2000), and 17 adults with severe-to-profound visual impairment crossed a virtual street in a head-mounted display. Four complexity levels ranged from an empty street to yielding vehicles with pedestrian avatars; only the two most complex levels contained moving vehicles. Cumulative absolute head yaw and latency to step-off were analyzed with mixed-effects models, and latencies were fitted with an ex-Gaussian distribution. lens.title: When to use the Bonferroni correction.
lens.summary: PURPOSE: The Bonferroni correction adjusts probability (p) values because of the increased risk of a type I error when making multiple statistical tests. The routine use of this test has been criticised as deleterious to sound statistical judgment, testing the wrong hypothesis, and reducing the chance of a type I error but at the expense  …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: The Bonferroni correction adjusts probability (p) values because of the increased risk of a type I error when making multiple statistical tests. The routine use of this test has been criticised as deleterious to sound statistical judgment, testing the wrong hypothesis, and reducing the chance of a type I error but at the expense of a type II error; yet it remains popular in ophthalmic research. The purpose of this article was to survey the use of the Bonferroni correction in research articles published in three optometric journals, viz. Ophthalmic & Physiological Optics, Optometry & Vision Science, and Clinical & Experimental Optometry, and to provide advice to authors contemplating multiple testing. RECENT FINDINGS: Some authors ignored the problem of multiple testing while others used the method uncritically with no rationale or discussion. A variety of methods of correcting p

lens.title: Presbyopia: Effectiveness of correction strategies.
lens.summary: Presbyopia is a global problem affecting over a billion people worldwide. The prevalence of unmanaged presbyopia is as high as 50% of those over 50 years of age in developing world populations, due to a lack of awareness and accessibility to affordable treatment, and is even as high as 34% in developed countries. …
lens.abstract: Presbyopia is a global problem affecting over a billion people worldwide. The prevalence of unmanaged presbyopia is as high as 50% of those over 50 years of age in developing world populations, due to a lack of awareness and accessibility to affordable treatment, and is even as high as 34% in developed countries. Definitions of presbyopia are inconsistent and varied, so we propose a redefinition that states "presbyopia occurs when the physiologically normal age-related reduction in the eye's focusing range reaches a point, when optimally corrected for distance vision, that the clarity of vision at near is insufficient to satisfy an individual's requirements". lens.title: Global Prevalence of Presbyopia and Vision Impairment from Uncorrected Presbyopia: Systematic Review, Meta-analysis, and Modelling.
lens.summary: There is a significant burden of VI from uncorrected presbyopia, with the greatest burden in rural areas of low-resource countries.
lens.abstract: TOPIC: Presbyopia prevalence and spectacle-correction coverage were estimated by systematic review and meta-analysis of epidemiologic evidence, then modeled to expand to country, region, and global estimates. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Understanding presbyopia epidemiologic factors and correction coverage is critical to overcoming the burden of vision impairment (VI) from uncorrected presbyopia. METHODS: We performed systematic reviews of presbyopia prevalence and spectacle-correction coverage. Accepted presbyopia prevalence data were gathered into 5-year age groups from 0 to 90 years or older and meta-analyzed within World Health Organization global burden of disease regions. We developed a model based on amplitude of accommodation adjusted for myopia rates to match the regionally meta-analyzed presbyopia prevalence. lens.title: Wavefront refraction and correction.
Corrective response times in a coordinated eye-head-arm countermanding task.
lens.summary: Inhibition of motor responses has been described as a race between two competing decision processes of motor initiation and inhibition, which manifest as the reaction time (RT) and the stop signal reaction time (SSRT); in the case where motor initiation wins out over inhibition, an erroneous movement occurs that usually needs to be correc …
lens.abstract: Inhibition of motor responses has been described as a race between two competing decision processes of motor initiation and inhibition, which manifest as the reaction time (RT) and the stop signal reaction time (SSRT); in the case where motor initiation wins out over inhibition, an erroneous movement occurs that usually needs to be corrected, leading to corrective response times (CRTs). Here we used a combined eye-head-arm movement countermanding task to investigate the mechanisms governing multiple effector coordination and the timing of corrective responses. We found a high degree of correlation between effector response times for RT, SSRT, and CRT, suggesting that decision processes are strongly dependent across effectors. lens.title: Lens-based surgical correction of presbyopia. Where are we in 2020?
lens.summary: It is necessary to know the variety of lenses available, and to have an in-depth understanding of their optical properties, as well as the impact that these will have later on their clinical performance and on the visual quality of the patients. This should help us to select the best alternative for each of them.
lens.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Presbyopia is the progressive and irreversible loss of accommodation due to aging. It is one of the main causes of loss of quality of life in people from 45 years of age, due to the, often novel, dependence on spectacles. The eagerness to correct it by ophthalmologists impulsed by the desire of millions of people who suffer from it, has become one of the main drivers for the development of intraocular lens (IOL) technology over the last twenty years. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This review briefly presents the different alternatives that have allowed us to improve the crystalline lens surgical approach of presbyopia; from monofocal lenses and monovision technique, accommodative, refractive, and diffractive multifocal lenses, and finally the most recent extended depth of focus/field lenses known as EDOFs. lens.title: How to Fix a Leaky Pipe.
Outcomes of presbyopia-correcting intraocular lenses after laser in situ keratomileusis.
lens.summary: In conclusion, in post-myopic LASIK eyes, AT LISA tri839MP provides a good visual outcome at both near and distance, but is more predictable at near than at distance. There is a myopic shift in the postoperative SE. Visual quality is satisfactory and has not been exacerbated. …
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) is the most common refractive surgery in young patients, which aims at providing a clear distance vision without the use of spectacles. With time, these patients develop symptomatic cataract, which affects activities of daily living, and to improve visual acuity, intraocular lens (IOL) implantation can be considered. In post-myopic LASIK patients, to allow continuation of spectacle independence, the implantation of presbyopia-correcting IOLs is a suitable option. The purpose of this retrospective case series is to report the visual outcome and quality in post-myopic LASIK eyes after the implantation of AT LISA tri839MP IOL. METHOD: Twenty eyes of 13 patients with history of myopic LASIK within 20 years underwent phacoemulsification by one single surgeon. All eyes were implanted with AT LISA tri839PMP IOL, and their outcomes were evaluated

lens.title: Visual and Physiological Optics: where will the journey lead us in 10 years?
The measurement of visual acuity in children: an evidence-based update.
lens.summary: Over the past decade, a number of large clinical trials have provided important information relating to the reliability and repeatability of commonly used paediatric tests of vision and their role in the diagnosis and management of paediatric ocular diseases. …
lens.abstract: Over the past decade, a number of large clinical trials have provided important information relating to the reliability and repeatability of commonly used paediatric tests of vision and their role in the diagnosis and management of paediatric ocular diseases. The aim of this review is to summarise recent findings on the use of paediatric visual acuity tests in clinical practice and to discuss the validity and accuracy of visual acuity measurements in infants and young children. We provide a broad overview of the benefits and challenges of measuring visual acuity in children and then discuss age-appropriate tests for measuring visual acuity in infants through to school-age children. We also discuss normative values for visual acuity in each age group and, where possible, provide comparisons of results between tests with a particular focus on the importance of optotype design.

lens.title: Regional differences in vision health: findings from Mwanza, Tanzania.
lens.summary: Due to regional differences in visual functioning in Mwanza, a national effort for vision health cannot be entirely successful without addressing the individualized needs of local communities. Reducing the cost of vision care appointments may expand vision health care utilization in Mwanza.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Visual impairment in developing countries has both social and economic impact on individuals and communities. Understanding the subjective visual functioning of populations will allow for local policymakers to identify the need for optometric or ophthalmic services in their communities. METHODS: The authors surveyed 644 adult patients in Mwanza, Tanzania at three clinics (Buzuruga, Mwananchi and Kisesa) using a modified Visual Functioning Questionnaire 25. Responses were categorized into General health, General vision, Ocular pain, Near activities, Distance activities, Social function, Mental health, Role difficulties, Color vision, Peripheral vision and Dependency. RESULTS: Patients at Buzuruga reported the lowest scores on most subscales. Of 100 employed patients, 37% claimed to have at least some difficulty in performing job duties due to their eyesight. lens.title: Optometry Research Agenda for the Next Decade: 20/20 by 2030.
Quality indicators in a community optometrist led cataract shared care scheme.
lens.summary: Direct cataract referrals from accredited community optometrists led to a majority of patients receiving a definitive clinical decision during first consultation. Postoperative community follow up reduced hospital visits and allowed for convenient consultation closer to home following uncomplicated cataract surgery. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Cataract shared care schemes involving community optometrists show wide variation in practice. We report on defined key performance indicators (KPIs) which improve accountability between stakeholders. METHODS: In this prospective study over nine months at a UK public hospital, we evaluated the outcomes of consecutive direct cataract referrals from community optometrists against two KPIs agreed under a service-level agreement between the Hospital Eye Service and community optometrists: (1) 85% of patients listed for cataract listing at first consultation; and (2) 90% postoperative feedback return rate on patients discharged to community optometrists. A detailed analysis on referral triage, surgical listing and postoperative form return rate is reported in this study. lens.title: Bifocal and Multifocal Contact Lenses for Presbyopia and Myopia Control.
lens.summary: Bifocal and multifocal optical devices are intended to get images into focus from objects placed at different distances from the observer. Spectacles, contact lenses, and intraocular lenses can meet the requirements to provide such a solution. …
lens.abstract: Bifocal and multifocal optical devices are intended to get images into focus from objects placed at different distances from the observer. Spectacles, contact lenses, and intraocular lenses can meet the requirements to provide such a solution. Contact lenses provide unique characteristics as a platform for implementing bifocality and multifocality. Compared to spectacles, they are closer to the eye, providing a wider field of view, less distortion, and their use is more consistent as they are not so easily removed along the day. In addition, contact lenses are also minimally invasive, can be easily exchangeable, and, therefore, suitable for conditions in which surgical procedures are not indicated. lens.title: Correction of presbyopia: old problems with old (and new) solutions.
lens.summary: We live in a three-dimensional world and the human eye can focus images from a wide range of distances by adjusting the power of the eye's lens (accommodation). Progressive senescent changes in the lens ultimately lead to a complete loss of this ability by about age 50, which then requires alternative strategies to generate high-quality r …
lens.abstract: We live in a three-dimensional world and the human eye can focus images from a wide range of distances by adjusting the power of the eye's lens (accommodation). Progressive senescent changes in the lens ultimately lead to a complete loss of this ability by about age 50, which then requires alternative strategies to generate high-quality retinal images for far and close viewing distances. This review paper highlights the biomimetic properties and underlying optical mechanisms of induced anisometropia, small apertures, dynamic lenses, and multi-optic lenses in ameliorating the visual consequences of presbyopia. Specifically, the advantages and consequences of non-liner neural summation leveraged in monovision treatments are reviewed. lens.title: "I can see fine": patient knowledge of eye care.
lens.summary: This study found notable gaps in knowledge of eye care and sight risks. If these gaps result in fewer eye examinations, they potentially contribute to increased risk of vision loss due to later stage detection. The results provide motivation for further study and development of effective public health education strategies.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To learn more about the perceptions and attitudes toward eye care of members of the public - in particular, their knowledge of the purpose, components and providers of eye examinations, their ability to self-monitor ocular status and their awareness of major sight threatening eye conditions. METHODS: This study used the qualitative research strategy, grounded theory. Participants were recruited via poster and social media. Two researchers, one with optometric knowledge and one without, moderated seven 60- to 90-min, semi-structured focus group discussions, which were audiotaped and transcribed. Participants also completed a short demographic questionnaire. Three researchers employed constant comparative coding strategies to identify common themes within the focus group transcripts. lens.title: Marketing and anecdotal evidence should not guide the delivery of optometric interventions.
The challenges of providing eye care for adults with intellectual disabilities.
lens.summary: This review is intended to raise awareness of the importance of providing high-quality eye care for people with intellectual disabilities and the increasing need for this eye care to be community-based. …
lens.abstract: This review is intended to raise awareness of the importance of providing high-quality eye care for people with intellectual disabilities and the increasing need for this eye care to be community-based. We describe the challenges to the provision of high-quality community-based eye care for people with intellectual disabilities and ideas, evidence and methods for overcoming them. The prevalence of visual impairment in people with intellectual disabilities has been reported to be at least 40 per cent, rising to as high as 100 per cent in those with profound and severe disabilities. A progressive move toward deinstitutionalisation has shifted the provision of care for people with intellectual disabilities. Individuals can have the freedom to access health-care services of their choice. This has posed challenges to the health-care system, including how to deliver high-quality community-base

lens.title: Macroeconomic landscape of refractive surgery in the United States.
lens.summary: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review examines the economic history of refractive surgery and the decline of laser-assisted in-situ keratomileusis (LASIK) in the USA, and the emergence of refractive cataract surgery as an area of growth. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review examines the economic history of refractive surgery and the decline of laser-assisted in-situ keratomileusis (LASIK) in the USA, and the emergence of refractive cataract surgery as an area of growth. RECENT FINDINGS: Since it peaked in 2007 at 1.4 million procedures per year, LASIK has declined 50% in the USA, whereas refractive cataract surgery, including presbyopia-correcting intraocular lenses (IOLs), astigmatism-correcting IOLs, and femtosecond laser-assisted cataract surgery, has grown to 350 000 procedures per year, beginning in 2003. SUMMARY: Patients are price-sensitive and responsive to publicity (good or bad) about refractive surgery and refractive cataract surgery. lens.title: Impact of monovision on dynamic accommodation of early presbyopes.
lens.summary: As the stimulus was abruptly changed from the retinal conjugate plane of the distance corrected eye to that of the near corrected eye, most early presbyopes fit with monovision accommodated, which resulted in a decline, not an increase in image quality in the near corrected eye. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To examine the impact of monovision on dynamic changes in accommodation, pupil responses, spherical aberration and resultant image quality in early presbyopes. METHODS: Refractive state, pupil size and spherical aberration levels were monitored in nine early presbyopes who exhibited some accommodation (40-50 years, mean = 42 ± 2.37 years) using a Shack-Hartmann aberrometer as a binocularly viewed stimulus stepped closer (from 2 m to 40 cm), or farther (from 40 cm to 2 m). Comparison data from two fully presbyopic (i.e. non-accommodating) subjects (ages 46 and 61 years) and two young adults (ages 26 and 29 years) were also collected. Each subject was fit with four different refractive strategies: (1) both eyes corrected for 2 m, (2) both eyes corrected for 40 cm, (3) monovision with the measured right eye corrected for 2 m and, (4) monovision with the right eye corrected for 40 c

lens.title: A novel rat head gaze determination system based on optomotor responses.
lens.summary: The optomotor response of animals is commonly used to measure their visual performance, e.g., rats of different genetically altered strains or various drug tests. With the presentation of stimuli using computer screens or projectors, the common idea focuses on measuring the eye movement or head and/or body movement to characterize changes …
lens.abstract: The optomotor response of animals is commonly used to measure their visual performance, e.g., rats of different genetically altered strains or various drug tests. With the presentation of stimuli using computer screens or projectors, the common idea focuses on measuring the eye movement or head and/or body movement to characterize changes of the head gaze. However, traditional methods rely on either the invasive fixation of animals, or the judgment of a human observer who reports the stimulus-tracking movements. In this paper, we propose a novel head gaze determination system to automatically track the head movement of rats without artificial markers. The experiments were done to demonstrate the process of optimizing parameters in image processing. lens.title: Modern spectacle lens design.
lens.summary: Ophthalmic lens design concerns the control of spectacle lens aberrations which occur when the eye rotates away from the optical centre of the lens. The most significant aberrations are oblique astigmatism and mean oblique error (power error). …
lens.abstract: Ophthalmic lens design concerns the control of spectacle lens aberrations which occur when the eye rotates away from the optical centre of the lens. The most significant aberrations are oblique astigmatism and mean oblique error (power error). A brief review of these aberrations is given, explaining how the lens designer can control them using just the bending of the lens, and what results can be achieved using simple spherical and toroidal surfaces. Before 1985, aspherical surfaces were used only for post-cataract spectacle lenses and high-power magnifiers. Today, aspherical surfaces are used by all major lens manufacturers to produce thinner, lighter and more attractive best-form lenses in the normal power range. lens.title: Impact of supervised student optometry consultations on the patient experience.
lens.summary: The findings of this study suggest that most patients view supervised student involvement in their optometric care as an important and highly positive experience. However, efforts should be made to avoid excessively long consultations and prolonged testing. …
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Understanding patient perceptions of having students involved in their clinical care is important as we strive to develop optimal models of care that integrate teaching with the best possible experience for the patient. The aim was to ascertain the impact of supervised optometry student consultations on the patient experience. METHODS: A survey comprising 45 questions was mailed to consecutive adult patients who had undergone a comprehensive eye examination at the Australian College of Optometry over a four-week period. RESULTS: Responses were received from 193 patients who had a student involved in their care (44 per cent response rate; 156 completed correctly) and 177 who did not have a student involved (32 per cent response rate; 105 completed correctly). lens.title: Stereoscopic Viewing Can Induce Changes in the CA/C Ratio.
lens.summary: These findings demonstrated that the CA/C ratio can exhibit adaptive adjustments. The observed nature and amount of the oculomotor modification failed to compensate for the stereoscopic constraint.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Stereoscopic displays challenge the neural cross-coupling between accommodation and vergence by inducing a constant accommodative demand and a varying vergence demand. Stereoscopic viewing calls for a decrease in the gain of vergence accommodation, which is the accommodation caused by vergence, quantified by using the convergence-accommodation to convergence (CA/C) ratio. However, its adaptability is still a subject of debate. METHODS: Cross-coupling (CA/C and AC/A ratios) and tonic components of vergence and accommodation were assessed in 12 participants (27.5 ± 5 years, stereoacuity better than 60 arc seconds, 6/6 acuity with corrected refractive error) before and after a 20-minute exposure to stereoscopic viewing. lens.title: Measuring visual acuity is not as simple as it seems.
Vision screening for children 36 to <72 months: recommended practices.
lens.summary: The National Expert Panel recommends that children aged 36 to younger than 72 months be screened annually (best practice) or at least once (accepted minimum standard) using one of the best practice approaches. Technological updates will be maintained at http://nationalcenter.preventblindness.org.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: This article provides recommendations for screening children aged 36 to younger than 72 months for eye and visual system disorders. The recommendations were developed by the National Expert Panel to the National Center for Children's Vision and Eye Health, sponsored by Prevent Blindness, and funded by the Maternal and Child Health Bureau of the Health Resources and Services Administration, United States Department of Health and Human Services. The recommendations describe both best and acceptable practice standards. Targeted vision disorders for screening are primarily amblyopia, strabismus, significant refractive error, and associated risk factors. The recommended screening tests are intended for use by lay screeners, nurses, and other personnel who screen children in educational, community, public health, or primary health care settings. lens.title: Visual system disorders and musculoskeletal neck complaints: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
lens.summary: Accommodation disorders and nonstrabismic binocular dysfunctions affect patients' binocular system and visual performance. These visual disorders could be associated with musculoskeletal discomfort in the neck and shoulder area. …
lens.abstract: Accommodation disorders and nonstrabismic binocular dysfunctions affect patients' binocular system and visual performance. These visual disorders could be associated with musculoskeletal discomfort in the neck and shoulder area. The purpose of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to ascertain the relationship between visual system disorders and the musculoskeletal system of the neck. The review protocol is available in PROSPERO (CRD42018112771). All articles selected examined the relationship between neck conditions (chronic neck pain and whiplash) and the visual system in adult populations. Studies with optometric or physiotherapeutic measurements were included. Bias risk was evaluated with the modified Cochrane Collaboration Tool and Study Quality Assessment Tool. To provide complete quality assessment evidence, the authors applied the GRADEpro Guideline Development Tool. The l

lens.title: A Review of Pharmacological Presbyopia Treatment.
lens.summary: Presbyopia reduces an individual's ability to perform visual tasks at near distances. It is a global problem, affecting over a billion people worldwide. Contact lenses, glasses, refractive surgery, and intraocular lens surgery are the main modalities in presbyopia treatment, although they all have some disadvantages. …
lens.abstract: Presbyopia reduces an individual's ability to perform visual tasks at near distances. It is a global problem, affecting over a billion people worldwide. Contact lenses, glasses, refractive surgery, and intraocular lens surgery are the main modalities in presbyopia treatment, although they all have some disadvantages. Thus, there is an increasing need for effective, easy-to-use, and noninvasive approaches for treating presbyopia while not limiting patients' daily activities. Pharmacological presbyopia treatment as an alternative method has been under investigation in recent years. We reviewed all relevant articles using the keywords "presbyopia," "presbyopia treatment," "pharmacological presbyopia treatment," and "presbyopic corrections" from 2010 to February 9, 2020, and summarized the main results of clinical trials, investigating the drops used for presbyopia treatment.

lens.title: Paediatric vision screening by non-healthcare volunteers: evidence based practices.
lens.summary: Non-healthcare professionals can be trained to an acceptable degree of accuracy to perform vision screening tests on children, which may assist in mitigating existing gaps in paediatric eye care.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: The purpose of this study was to test the sensitivity and specificity of eight undergraduate volunteer examiners conducting vision screening tests in a community setting, in order to determine if non-eye care professionals were able to be trained to an appropriate level of skill. METHODS: Eight undergraduate volunteer examiners were trained to conduct vision screening tests to address a gap in pediatric community eye care. Phase I of the study was implemented in the pediatric ophthalmology clinic, and phase II was conducted in nine local schools. Phase I consisted of 40 h of training for each volunteer regarding specific vision tests. Phase II consisted of screening children at nine local schools. lens.title: Monovision and the Misperception of Motion.
lens.summary: Monovision is a common prescription lens correction for presbyopia [1]. Each eye is corrected for a different distance, causing one image to be blurrier than the other. Millions of people have monovision corrections, but little is known about how interocular blur differences affect motion perception. …
lens.abstract: Monovision is a common prescription lens correction for presbyopia [1]. Each eye is corrected for a different distance, causing one image to be blurrier than the other. Millions of people have monovision corrections, but little is known about how interocular blur differences affect motion perception. Here, we report that blur differences cause a previously unknown motion illusion that makes people dramatically misperceive the distance and three-dimensional direction of moving objects. The effect occurs because the blurry and sharp images are processed at different speeds. For moving objects, the mismatch in processing speed causes a neural disparity, which results in the misperceptions. lens.title: Optometry in Nepalese Context: The Profession Beyond Providing Refraction Services.
lens.summary: Optometry is an independent profession which is specialised for providing comprehensive eye care including refraction and dispensing services, diagnosis and management of eye diseases and visual rehabilitation. …
lens.abstract: Optometry is an independent profession which is specialised for providing comprehensive eye care including refraction and dispensing services, diagnosis and management of eye diseases and visual rehabilitation. In clinical settings of Nepal, optometrists are primarily recognised as refractionists and are provided with working opportunities in the same area. This report highlights other optometric services such as binocular vision, multifocal lenses, contact lenses and occupational lens design which can be provided by optometrists besides performing refraction and prescribing spectacles. Considering large proportion of optometrists with further education and being working outside the country, new specialised services can be introduced through training and workshop to the fellow optometrists so that specialised services can reach up to the public level. lens.title: Visualization of Light Propagation with Multifocal Intraocular Lenses Using the Ouzo Effect.
lens.summary: The number of presbyopia correcting intraocular lenses (IOLs) is increasing and new technologies are constantly emerging with the aim of correcting the loss of accommodation after cataract surgery. Various optical designs have been proposed to implement multifocality or an extended depth of focus (EDOF). …
lens.abstract: The number of presbyopia correcting intraocular lenses (IOLs) is increasing and new technologies are constantly emerging with the aim of correcting the loss of accommodation after cataract surgery. Various optical designs have been proposed to implement multifocality or an extended depth of focus (EDOF). Depending on the optical principle of an implanted lens, the visual performance often is deteriorated by superposition of individual image planes and halos of varying intensity. This experimental study presents a concept to visualize the light fields and especially the halos of mono- and multifocal IOLs using the well known alcoholic beverage "ouzo" in order to obtain qualitative data on the imaging characteristics. lens.title: The advantages of intermediate-tier, inter-optometric referral of low risk pigmented lesions.
lens.summary: Intermediate-tier optometric eye-care in pigmented lesions (following opportunistic primary care screening) has the potential to reduce the number of cases with non-specific diagnoses and to increase those with less common diagnoses. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Pigmented ocular lesions are commonly encountered by eye-care professionals, and range from benign to sight or life-threatening. After identifying a lesion, the primary care professional must establish the likely diagnosis and decide either to reassure, to monitor or to refer. The increasing use of ocular imaging technologies has contributed to an increase in the detection rate of pigmented lesions and a higher number of referrals, which may challenge existing pathways of health-care delivery. Specialist services may be over-burdened by referring all patients with pigmented lesions for an opinion, while inter-optometric referrals are underutilised. The aim of this study was to describe the referral patterns of pigmented lesions to an optometry led intermediate-tier collaborative care clinic. lens.title: Examination Practices and Referral of Patients With Diabetic Retinopathy by Optometrists in Routine Clinical Care.
lens.summary: Although DFE was performed reliably by optometrists, utilization of imaging, DR grading and coding, and appropriate follow-up periods could be improved. [Ophthalmic Surg Lasers Imaging Retina. 2019;50:608-612.].
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: To analyze the examination practices and referral of patients with diabetic retinopathy (DR) by optometrists in routine clinical care. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Diabetic patient records from 2012 to 2018 were retrospectively reviewed for documentation of dilated fundus exam (DFE), imaging, follow-up appointments, and referrals. Concordance between clinical exam and coding was also analyzed. RESULTS: For 97.8% of encounters, DFE was performed, the patient was referred for DFE, or DFE was scheduled for follow-up. When DFE was performed at the initial visit, this resulted in referral of 19.8% of patients to an ophthalmologist. Imaging was obtained occasionally, with fundus photos in 2.6% and optical coherence tomography in 14.5% of encounters. Concordance of DR grading between exam and coding was 78.8%. lens.title: Care pathways for glaucoma detection and monitoring in the UK.
lens.summary: Glaucoma presents considerable challenges in providing clinically and cost-effective care pathways. While UK population screening is not seen as justifiable, arrangements for case finding have historically been considered relatively ineffective. …
lens.abstract: Glaucoma presents considerable challenges in providing clinically and cost-effective care pathways. While UK population screening is not seen as justifiable, arrangements for case finding have historically been considered relatively ineffective. Detection challenges include an undetected disease burden, whether from populations failing to access services or difficulties in delivering effective case-finding strategies, and a high false positive rate from referrals via traditional case finding pathways. The enhanced General Ophthalmic Service (GOS) in Scotland and locally commissioned glaucoma referral filtering services (GRFS) elsewhere have undoubtedly reduced false positive referrals, and there is emerging evidence of effectiveness of these pathways. lens.title: Multi-meridional keratometry.
lens.summary: During conventional keratometry, the two principal meridia are identified and measurements of the anterior corneal curvature determined along these orientations. However, in cases of corneal irregularity, the principal meridia may be difficult to identify. …
lens.abstract: During conventional keratometry, the two principal meridia are identified and measurements of the anterior corneal curvature determined along these orientations. However, in cases of corneal irregularity, the principal meridia may be difficult to identify. Accordingly, the present study sought to evaluate two alternative procedures which do not require identification of the principal meridia. Instead, measurements of anterior corneal curvature were determined along either three or four preselected meridia and subsequently converted into the standard format for measurements of anterior corneal curvature. The study was performed on 25 visually normal subjects and the results compared with conventional two meridian keratometry findings. Glaucoma: reporting back.
How often are spectacles prescribed to "normal" preschool children?
lens.summary: While some preschoolers without amblyogenic factors may require spectacle correction, a significant percentage of children are probably prescribed glasses unnecessarily. Extrapolation of these data to the United States population suggests that a single mandatory eye examination prior to school entry could cost over 200,000,000 US dollars  …
lens.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Legislation to require formal eye examination prior to school entry is being considered in several states and is supported by optical trade organizations. Pediatric ophthalmologists cite anecdotal cases that suggest children receive spectacles unnecessarily, but data to support this are lacking. METHODS: Eye examination results from children referred to local eye doctors following a statewide preschool photoscreening program were reviewed to determine how often glasses were prescribed for children who did not have amblyogenic factors (those with false-positive screenings). RESULTS: Of 102,508 preschool children screened, 890 children did not have amblyogenic factors (false-positive screenings). Nevertheless, spectacles were prescribed for 174 (19.5%) of these children. lens.title: The effect of experience on the detection of small eye movements.
lens.summary: The results indicate that during ideal conditions, little or no training is required for efficient detection of small eye movements.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to determine whether experience improves detection of small eye movements similar to those seen in the cover test during ideal conditions. METHODS: Three groups of examiners with varying amounts of experience in eye movement detection tasks were studied. Eight examiners were 1st-year optometry students, six were 4th-year optometry students, and six were practicing optometrists. To determine thresholds for eye movement detection, examiners indicated the horizontal direction in which the eyes of one of the experimenters moved. The direction and extent of each eye movement was randomly selected. The extent of the eye movement was one of eight logarithmic steps from a maximum that was determined through an initial session where the approximate sensitivity of the examiners was found (generally +/- 1.75 prism diopters). lens.title: Predicting prescribed magnification.
lens.summary: The magnification necessary to perform normal visual tasks can be predicted in the majority of cases using visual acuity measures, although measuring the effect of proximal magnification demonstrates the effect of stronger glasses and identifies those in whom prescribed magnification is more difficult to predict.
lens.abstract: AIM: To determine the best method of estimating the optimum magnification needed by visually impaired patients. METHODS: The magnification of low vision aids prescribed to 187 presbyopic visually impaired patients for reading newspapers or books was compared with logMAR distance and near acuity (at 25 cm) and magnification predicted by +4 D step near additions. RESULTS: Distance letter (r = 0.58) and near word visual acuity (r = 0.67) were strongly correlated to the prescribed magnification as were predictive formulae based on these measures. Prediction using the effect of proximal magnification resulted in a similar correlation (r = 0.67) and prediction was poorer in those who did not benefit from proximal magnification. lens.title: Item banking: a generational change in patient-reported outcome measurement.
lens.summary: Item banks for the measurement of the latent traits of VRAL, symptoms, and QOL have been formed. New items can be added to enable evolution of measurement. Item banking facilitates accurate and precise measurement through computer adaptive testing. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Patient-reported outcomes are traditionally measured with questionnaires and many have been developed to measure Vision-Related Activity Limitation (VRAL; visual disability or visual functioning), Symptoms, and Quality Of Life (QOL). These vary in quality and can be classified as First or Second Generation instruments. First generation instruments are characterized by simple summary scoring of ordinal responses, which precludes interval measurement. This problem is solved in second generation instruments where Rasch analysis is used to optimize psychometric properties. However, second generation instruments retain limitations; difficulties in comparing scores across instruments, limited applicability to populations and inability to adapt to change. Mean values are provided for these ages in optometric tests that directly assess the vergence system, horizontal phorias for near and far vision (measured by a modified version of the Thorington method), negative and positive vergence amplitude for near and far vision (step vergence testing), vergence facility (flippers 8 Delta BI/8 Delta BO), and near-point of convergence (penlight push-up technique and red-lens push-up technique), as well as stimulus accommodative convergence/accommodation ratio and stereoacuity (Randot test) which provide an overall evaluation of the vergence, accommodative and oculomotor systems. lens.title: Orthokeratology review and update.
lens.summary: Orthokeratology (OK) is a clinical technique that uses specially designed rigid contact lenses to reshape the cornea to temporarily reduce or eliminate refractive error. This article reviews the history of traditional daily-wear OK (1960s to 1980s) and discusses the reasons for the recent resurgence in interest in the new modality of over …
lens.abstract: Orthokeratology (OK) is a clinical technique that uses specially designed rigid contact lenses to reshape the cornea to temporarily reduce or eliminate refractive error. This article reviews the history of traditional daily-wear OK (1960s to 1980s) and discusses the reasons for the recent resurgence in interest in the new modality of overnight OK, using reverse-geometry lens designs (1990s to the present). The clinical efficacy of the current procedure is examined and outcomes from clinical studies in terms of refractive error change and unaided visual acuity are summarised. Onset of the effects of overnight OK lens wear is rapid, with most change after the first night of lens wear and stability of refractive change after seven to 10 days. lens.title: Assessment of inherited colour vision defects in clinical practice.
lens.summary: Optometrists should test the colour vision of all new patients with the Ishihara and Richmond HRR (2002) tests. Those shown to have CVD should be assessed with the Medmont C-100 test and the Farnsworth D15 test and given appropriate advice based on the test results.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Colour vision deficiency (CVD) has a high prevalence and is often a handicap in everyday life. Those who have CVD will be better able to adapt and make more informed career choices, if they know about their deficiency. The fact that from 20 to 30 per cent of adults with abnormal colour vision do not know they have CVD suggests that colour vision is not tested as often as it should be. This may be because of practitioner uncertainty about which tests to use, how to interpret them and the advice that should be given to patients on the basis of the results. The purpose of this paper is to recommend tests for primary care assessment of colour vision and provide guidance on the advice that can be given to patients with CVD. METHODS: The literature on colour vision tests and the relationship between the results of the tests and performance at practical colour tasks was reviewed. RE

lens.title: Communicating the ocular and systemic complications of obesity to patients.
lens.summary: Optometrists have a duty to educate and counsel their overweight and obese patients on the devastating ocular complications that could manifest as a result of obesity.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Obesity has become a growing worldwide epidemic that is associated with serious medical complications. Many clinicians and patients are aware of the systemic complications of obesity, but there are few providers and patients who are aware of the ocular manifestations of obesity. METHODS: A review of the current medical literature was performed. Ocular and systemic manifestations associated with obesity are described, and a methodology for educating the optometric patient is presented. RESULTS: There is significant morbidity and mortality associated with obesity, which is causing serious consequences to patients and an enormous economic strain on the health care system. lens.title: Accommodative instability: relationship to progression of early onset myopia.
lens.summary: The results presented in the present study suggest that instability of accommodation accompanies myopic progression, although a casual relationship cannot be established.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: In a previous study, we demonstrated that children with early onset myopia had greater instability of accommodation than a group of emmetropic children. Since that study was correlational, we were unable to determine the causal relationship between this and myopic progression. To address this, we examined the children two years later. We predicted that if accommodative instability was causing the myopic progression, instability at Visit 1 should predict the refractive error at Visit 2. Additionally, instability at Visit 1 should predict myopic progression. METHODS: Thirteen myopic and 16 emmetropic children were included in the analysis.
