lens.title: Decision making in chronic glaucoma--optometrists vs ophthalmologists in a shared care service.
lens.summary: An audit model of decision-making in shared care is demonstrated that in this case supported the apprenticeship model of training utilised in the clinic.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Shared care schemes have become popular in glaucoma management in the UK over the past 20 years. Published audits of decision making processes by non-ophthalmologists working in such schemes are however rare. Our aim was to audit the appropriateness of optometrists' decision-making when working in an in-house shared care glaucoma scheme. METHODS: A single masked comparison study utilising retrospective consensus decisions by two ophthalmologists compared with 'live' optometrist decisions from three optometrists who reviewed patients with glaucoma, suspect glaucoma and ocular hypertension. RESULTS: Comparisons were made on management decisions on 140 consecutive eligible patients. There were high degrees of agreement (>88%) in terms of visual field interpretation, medical and surgical management decisions, timing of next appointment and ordering of visual field tests. lens.abstract: A reduction in blood flow to the brain causes stroke and damage to neuronal networks. Cerebral ischemia is frequently associated with loss of visual functions. Because retinal and small cerebral vessels are vulnerable to similar risk factors, the loss of vision could result from concurrent retinal ischemia, and it is not clear if visual functions may be inhibited by cerebral ischemia directly. In this study, the distal middle cerebral artery in the right hemisphere of mice was occluded to produce unilateral cerebral ischemia and subsequent infarction. lens.title: The underachieving child.
lens.summary: Visual factors in specific learning difficulties (SpLD) are reviewed. People with SpLD fail to achieve at a level that is commensurate with their intelligence. The commonest SpLD is dyslexia, which usually results from phonological processing/decoding deficits. …
lens.abstract: Visual factors in specific learning difficulties (SpLD) are reviewed. People with SpLD fail to achieve at a level that is commensurate with their intelligence. The commonest SpLD is dyslexia, which usually results from phonological processing/decoding deficits. Additionally, there are several optometric correlates of SpLD which may, in some cases, contribute to the learning difficulty. These correlates include binocular instability and a low amplitude of accommodation. Some people with reading difficulties and perceptual distortions/eyestrain can be helped by individually prescribed coloured filters. A visual processing anomaly is also often present in the form of a deficit of the transient visual system. The role of the optometrist is discussed.

lens.title: Optic disc morphology--rethinking shape.
lens.summary: Morphometrics, a branch of morphology, represents the study of size and shape components of biological form and their variation in the population. Assessment of optic disc morphology is essential in the diagnosis and management of many ophthalmic disorders. …
lens.abstract: Morphometrics, a branch of morphology, represents the study of size and shape components of biological form and their variation in the population. Assessment of optic disc morphology is essential in the diagnosis and management of many ophthalmic disorders. Much work has been performed to characterize size-related parameters of the optic disc; however, limited information is available on shape variation in the general population. In contrast to optic disc or cup sizes, which are conceptually meaningful variables with a defined unit of measurement, there are few metric constructs by which to quantify, visualize and interpret variation in optic disc or cup shape. This has significance in ophthalmic diseases with a genetic basis as recent evidence has suggested that optic disc shape may be heritable. lens.title: Fitting children with glasses.
lens.summary: 1. When fitting children for glasses, the emphasis must always be on ensuring that the glasses not only correct the visual problems but also feel and look good. Otherwise, they will not be worn. 2. There is a great value in creating an atmosphere in an optical shop that makes children want to visit. …
lens.abstract: 1. When fitting children for glasses, the emphasis must always be on ensuring that the glasses not only correct the visual problems but also feel and look good. Otherwise, they will not be worn. 2. There is a great value in creating an atmosphere in an optical shop that makes children want to visit. The process of visiting and selecting glasses should be fun for a child. Children's theme sections or toys are an effective method of making a visit pleasurable for a child. 3. For all the extra features an optical shop may offer, perhaps the most special are the intangibles of patience, respect, and genuine affection.

lens.title: Evaluation of a prototype Minified Augmented-View device for patients with impaired night vision.
lens.summary: An evaluation was carried out of the first prototype (LV-3) of a new night vision device, which incorporates visual field expansion through minification (Minified Augmented-View), to provide feedback for continuing development. …
lens.abstract: An evaluation was carried out of the first prototype (LV-3) of a new night vision device, which incorporates visual field expansion through minification (Minified Augmented-View), to provide feedback for continuing development. Six subjects with night blindness completed visual function measurements and indoor mobility assessments without a device, with the LV-3 and with a commercially available comparison device (the Multi-Vision) at light levels representative of well lit and poorly lit streets. Device performance and potential benefits in real-world situations were evaluated at four outdoor locations (well lit to very dark). Results indicate that the see-through nature and spectacle-frame mounting of the LV-3 address some of the cosmetic and ergonomic disadvantages of currently available devices; however insufficient light sensitivity of the prototype camera limited LV-3 performance.

lens.title: The infant patient.
lens.summary: The infant patient presents a challenge to the optometrist who must structure an examination within the infant's limited capabilities and then manage a rapidly developing visual system. The present paper provides an overview of infant visual development and the visually guided behaviours expected during normal development. …
lens.abstract: The infant patient presents a challenge to the optometrist who must structure an examination within the infant's limited capabilities and then manage a rapidly developing visual system. The present paper provides an overview of infant visual development and the visually guided behaviours expected during normal development. Techniques for assessing vision in infant are reviewed and a recommendation is given for the optometric examination of infants. Some important urgencies, emergencies and causes of visual impairment are highlighted.

lens.summary: Hyperopia is the most common refractive error of children. However, children with moderate-to-high degrees of hyperopia are at significantly increased risk for the development of amblyopia and strabismus. …
lens.abstract: Hyperopia is the most common refractive error of children. Children with mild (or even moderate) levels of hyperopia usually do not experience visual problems resulting from this hyperopia. However, children with moderate-to-high degrees of hyperopia are at significantly increased risk for the development of amblyopia and strabismus. It is this association with these visually threatening disorders that makes hyperopia in children an important public health problem. In addition, even lesser degrees of hyperopia may affect the child's ability to perform well in near-related tasks, such as reading. The effect hyperopia has on an individual child is dependent on a variety of factors, including the magnitude of hyperopia, the age of the individual, the status of the accommodative and convergence system, and the demands placed on the visual system. lens.title: Prentice Award Lecture 2010: A case for peripheral optical treatment strategies for myopia.
lens.summary: It is well established that refractive development is regulated by visual feedback. However, most optical treatment strategies designed to reduce myopia progression have not produced the desired results, primarily because some of our assumptions concerning the operating characteristics of the vision-dependent mechanisms that regulate refr …
lens.abstract: It is well established that refractive development is regulated by visual feedback. However, most optical treatment strategies designed to reduce myopia progression have not produced the desired results, primarily because some of our assumptions concerning the operating characteristics of the vision-dependent mechanisms that regulate refractive development have been incorrect. In particular, because of the prominence of central vision in primates, it has generally been assumed that signals from the fovea determine the effects of vision on refractive development. However, experiments in laboratory animals demonstrate that ocular growth and emmetropization are mediated by local retinal mechanisms and that foveal vision is not essential for many vision-dependent aspects of refractive development. lens.title: Recent advances in measurement of monochromatic aberrations of human eyes.
lens.summary: The field of aberrations of the human eye is moving rapidly, being driven by the desire to monitor and optimise vision following refractive surgery. It is important for ophthalmologists and optometrists to have an understanding of the magnitude of various aberrations and how these are likely to be affected by refractive surgery and other  …
lens.abstract: The field of aberrations of the human eye is moving rapidly, being driven by the desire to monitor and optimise vision following refractive surgery. It is important for ophthalmologists and optometrists to have an understanding of the magnitude of various aberrations and how these are likely to be affected by refractive surgery and other corrections. In this paper, I consider methods used to measure aberrations, the magnitude of aberrations in general populations and how these are affected by various factors (for example, age, refractive error, accommodation and refractive surgery) and how aberrations and their correction affect spatial visual performance.

lens.title: New methods and techniques for sensing the wave aberrations of human eyes.
lens.summary: During the past decade, there has been a remarkable expansion of the application of wavefront-related technologies to the human eye. The ability to measure the wavefront aberrations (WA) of an individual eye has greatly improved our understanding on the optical properties of the human eye. …
lens.abstract: During the past decade, there has been a remarkable expansion of the application of wavefront-related technologies to the human eye. The ability to measure the wavefront aberrations (WA) of an individual eye has greatly improved our understanding on the optical properties of the human eye. The development of wavefront sensors has further generated an intensive effort to revise methods to correct vision. Wavefront sensors have offered the promise of a new generation of visual correction methods that can correct high order aberrations beyond defocus and astigmatism, that is, the wavefront-guided excimer laser platforms and adaptive optics, thus improving visual performance or fundus imaging at unprecedented spatial resolution. lens.title: Characteristics of low-vision rehabilitation services in the United States.
lens.summary: This census for the first time characterizes usual-care low-vision rehabilitation services in the United States for nonveteran adults.
lens.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To describe characteristics of services, providers, and patients in low-vision rehabilitation entities serving adults in the United States. METHODS: Entities (excluding Veterans Affairs clinics) were identified through professional associations, Web searches, and a telephone survey to retina practices. A census obtained information on entity types, provider types, rehabilitation services available, and clientele. Surveys were administered by telephone, fax, e-mail, or mail, whichever was preferred by the respondent. RESULTS: A total of 1228 low-vision rehabilitation service entities were identified, with 608 surveyed (49.5% response rate). Almost half (42.7%) were private optometry practices. lens.title: Background and history of autism in relation to vision care.
lens.summary: Although autism existed before 1943, it was Leo Kanner who is credited with the first detailed description of autistic behavior. Before Kanner's report, the behavior was generally known as childhood schizophrenia. …
lens.abstract: Although autism existed before 1943, it was Leo Kanner who is credited with the first detailed description of autistic behavior. Before Kanner's report, the behavior was generally known as childhood schizophrenia. He noted that the outstanding common feature of all the children was certain parental personalities, like obsessiveness and lack of warm-heartedness. Concurrent with Kanner's report and observations were those of Asperger in 1944. However, Asperger's report, in a German-language journal, was not brought to the forefront until the 1980s. The children described by Asperger had milder forms of behavior disorders than those described by Kanner, with the resulting diagnosis of autism broadened and blurred. The role of optometrists in India: an integral part of an eye health team.

lens.abstract: India has a proud tradition of blindness prevention, being the first country in the world to implement a blindness control programme which focused on a model to address blinding eye disease. However, with 133 million people blind or vision impaired due to the lack of an eye examination and provision of an appropriate pair of spectacles, it is imperative to establish a cadre of eye care professionals to work in conjunction with ophthalmologists to deliver comprehensive eye care. The integration of highly educated four year trained optometrists into primary health services is a practical means of correcting refractive error and detecting ocular disease, enabling co-managed care between ophthalmologists and optometrists. lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Eccentric photorefraction provides an opportunity to gather rapid and remote estimates of refraction and gaze position from infants. The technique has the potential for extensive use in vision screenings and studies of visual development. The goal of this study was to assess the refraction calibration of the PowerRefractor (Multichannel Systems) for use with uncyclopleged infants. METHODS: The defocus measurements from the instrument were compared with the results of simultaneous retinoscopy in one analysis and with known amounts of defocus induced with trial lenses in another. Data were collected from infants 1 to 6 months of age and adults. lens.abstract: Background The Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2017 (GBD 2017) includes a comprehensive assessment of incidence, prevalence, and years lived with disability (YLDs) for 354 causes in 195 countries and territories from 1990 to 2017. Previous GBD studies have shown how the decline of mortality rates from 1990 to 2016 has led to an increase in life expectancy, an ageing global population, and an expansion of the non-fatal burden of disease and injury. These studies have also shown how a substantial portion of the world's population experiences non-fatal health loss with considerable heterogeneity among different causes, locations, ages, and sexes. lens.abstract: Background Improving survival and extending the longevity of life for all populations requires timely, robust evidence on local mortality levels and trends. The Global Burden of Disease 2015 Study (GBD 2015) provides a comprehensive assessment of all-cause and cause-specific mortality for 249 causes in 195 countries and territories from 1980 to 2015. These results informed an in-depth investigation of observed and expected mortality patterns based on sociodemographic measures. Methods We estimated all-cause mortality by age, sex, geography, and year using an improved analytical approach originally developed for GBD 2013 and GBD 2010. Improvements included refinements to the estimation of child and adult mortality and corresponding uncertainty, parameter selection for under-5 mortality synthesis by spatiotemporal Gaussian process regression, and sibling history data processing. lens.abstract: Background Up-to-date evidence about levels and trends in disease and injury incidence, prevalence, and years lived with disability (YLDs) is an essential input into global, regional, and national health policies. In the Global Burden of Disease Study 2013 (GBD 2013), we estimated these quantities for acute and chronic diseases and injuries for 188 countries between 1990 and 2013. Methods Estimates were calculated for disease and injury incidence, prevalence, and YLDs using GBD 2010 methods with some important refinements. Results for incidence of acute disorders and prevalence of chronic disorders are new additions to the analysis. Key improvements include expansion to the cause and sequelae list, updated systematic reviews, use of detailed injury codes, improvements to the Bayesian meta-regression method (DisMod-MR), and use of severity splits for various causes. lens.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs), through their complex cargo, can reflect the state of their cell of origin and change the functions and phenotypes of other cells. These features indicate strong biomarker and therapeutic potential and have generated broad interest, as evidenced by the steady year-on-year increase in the numbers of scientific publications about EVs. Important advances have been made in EV metrology and in understanding and applying EV biology. However, hurdles remain to realising the potential of EVs in domains ranging from basic biology to clinical applications due to challenges in EV nomenclature, separation from non-vesicular extracellular particles, characterisation and functional studies. lens.abstract: Purpose Myopia is a common cause of vision loss, with uncorrected myopia the leading cause of distance vision impairment globally. Individual studies show variations in the prevalence of myopia and high myopia between regions and ethnic groups, and there continues to be uncertainty regarding increasing prevalence of myopia. Design Systematic review and meta-analysis. Methods We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of the prevalence of myopia and high myopia and estimated temporal trends from 2000 to 2050 using data published since 1995. The primary data were gathered into 5-year age groups from 0 to ≥100, in urban or rural populations in each country, standardized to definitions of myopia of -0.50 diopter (D) or less and of high myopia of -5.00 D or less, projected to the year 2010, then meta-analyzed within Global Burden of Disease (GBD) regions. lens.abstract: Background The Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2015 provides an up-to-date synthesis of the evidence for risk factor exposure and the attributable burden of disease. By providing national and subnational assessments spanning the past 25 years, this study can inform debates on the importance of addressing risks in context. Methods We used the comparative risk assessment framework developed for previous iterations of the Global Burden of Disease Study to estimate attributable deaths, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), and trends in exposure by age group, sex, year, and geography for 79 behavioural, environmental and occupational, and metabolic risks or clusters of risks from 1990 to 2015. lens.summary: Background Frailty can be measured in relation to the accumulation of deficits using a frailty index. A frailty index can be developed from most ageing databases. Our objective is to systematically describe a standard procedure for constructing a frailty index. …
lens.abstract: Background Frailty can be measured in relation to the accumulation of deficits using a frailty index. A frailty index can be developed from most ageing databases. Our objective is to systematically describe a standard procedure for constructing a frailty index. Methods This is a secondary analysis of the Yale Precipitating Events Project cohort study, based in New Haven CT. Non-disabled people aged 70 years or older (n = 754) were enrolled and re-contacted every 18 months. The database includes variables on function, cognition, co-morbidity, health attitudes and practices and physical performance measures. Data came from the baseline cohort and those available at the first 18-month follow-up assessment. Results Procedures for selecting health variables as candidate deficits were applied to yield 40 deficits. Recoding procedures were applied for categorical, ordinal and interval variables

refractive.title: Impact of Iris Color and Laterality on Lenticule Extraction Time in Keratorefractive Lenticule Extraction (KLEx).
refractive.summary: Purpose: This study aims to evaluate the effects of iris color and laterality on keratorefractive lenticule extraction (KLEx) surgery time. Setting: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 656 eyes of 328 patients undergoing small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE). Mean patient age was 32 ± 7 years. …
refractive.abstract: Purpose: This study aims to evaluate the effects of iris color and laterality on keratorefractive lenticule extraction (KLEx) surgery time. Setting: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 656 eyes of 328 patients undergoing small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE). Mean patient age was 32 ± 7 years. Methods: Preoperative parameters, including manifest refraction spherical equivalent (MRSE), refractive cylinder, and corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA), were measured. Iris color was classified as "light" (n = 390) or "dark" (n = 266) by a senior ophthalmologist as the grader. Surgical time was determined from video recordings, defined as the time between opening of the KLEx incision and extraction of the lenticule. refractive.title: Corneal haze after transepithelial vs. alcohol-assisted photorefractive keratectomy in myopia and myopic astigmatism: A retrospective study.
refractive.summary: Both TPRK and alcohol-assisted PRK are safe and effective for myopia and myopic astigmatism correction, with low risk of clinically significant haze and comparable long-term outcomes.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate and compare corneal haze, assessed both clinically and by corneal densitometry, after transepithelial photorefractive keratectomy (TPRK) versus alcohol-assisted PRK in myopic and myopic astigmatism patients, and to assess associated visual acuity and refractive outcomes over a 6-month follow-up. METHODS: A total of 106 eyes from 53 patients underwent PRK or TPRK without mitomycin C application, using the Teneo 317 excimer laser platform. All surgeries were performed by experienced surgeons following standardized protocols. Outcomes included Fantes clinical haze grading, Pentacam® corneal densitometry, uncorrected (UDVA) and best corrected distance visual acuity (BCVA), and manifest refraction, assessed at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively. refractive.title: A Preliminary Study on the Association of Mild Dry Eye with Corneal Biomechanical Properties and Early Refractive Outcomes After KLEx.
refractive.summary: Corneal stromal lenticule elastic modulus showed good discriminatory ability between the study groups. The perioperative management of corneal refractive surgery warrants particular attention in patients with concomitant dry eye.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSES: This study aimed to investigate the impact of mild dry eye on corneal biomechanical properties and early postoperative refractive outcomes after keratorefractive lenticule extraction (KLEx), and to examine the potential association between differences in corneal biomechanical properties and refractive outcomes. METHODS: This was a retrospective study with a relatively small sample size. Patients were divided into control and dry eye groups, and those undergoing KLEx were further divided into KLEx control and KLEx dry eye groups. Corneal biomechanical properties were assessed using Corvis ST and indentation testing. Differences in biomechanical parameters and postoperative refractive results were compared across all groups. refractive.title: Proportional conservation of vectorial non-summation in corneal astigmatism: a thick-lens analysis in normal and keratoconic eyes.
refractive.summary: Corneal astigmatism is not fully described by vector summation of the two surfaces. The residual, compatible with thick-lens coupling and device-specific optical conventions, is larger in absolute terms in keratoconus but represents a constant proportion of each eye's astigmatism across the ectatic spectrum. …
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To test whether the residual between ray-traced total corneal astigmatism and the vector sum of the anterior and posterior second-order astigmatic components is an independent, disease-related signal or a proportionally conserved feature of corneal thick-lens optics. METHODS: Secondary analysis of a deidentified multicenter database of unoperated eyes examined with Pentacam HR and Corvis ST, restricted to clinically normal eyes and bilateral keratoconus, one eye per subject (1,680 normal; 1,181 keratoconic). Second-order Zernike astigmatic vectors were extracted over a 6.0 mm zone for the anterior (F) and posterior (B) surfaces and the ray-traced total cornea (T). The primary endpoint was the non-summation magnitude |T-F-B|. refractive.title: Clinical Outcomes of Implantable Collamer Lens Implantation Versus Photorefractive Keratectomy for Myopic Regression After Laser Vision Correction.
refractive.summary: Both ICL implantation and PRK are effective and safe for treating myopic regression after LVC. However, ICL implantation provides more rapid visual recovery during the early postoperative period, while both modalities yield comparable 6-month refractive predictability.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: Myopic regression is a common complication after laser vision correction (LVC). While photorefractive keratectomy (PRK) and implantable collamer lens (ICL) implantation are considered effective retreatment options with favorable outcomes, no direct comparative study has evaluated these two modalities for treating regression. Therefore, we aimed to compare the clinical outcomes of ICL implantation and PRK in patients with myopic regression after LVC. METHODS: This retrospective study compared 30 eyes treated with ICL implantation and 24 eyes with transepithelial PRK as retreatment for myopic regression after prior LVC. Clinical outcomes were evaluated over a 6-month follow-up period. RESULTS: At 6 months, 100% of eyes in both groups achieved a postoperative spherical equivalent (SE) within ±1.00 D of the intended target, with uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA) of 20/20 or

refractive.title: Evaluation of effective optical zone following SMILE and FS-LASIK treatment for myopia and myopic astigmatism: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
refractive.summary: EOZ/POZ after corneal refractive surgery depends on surgical technique, magnitude of refractive correction, and the method used to estimate EOZ; SMILE consistently provides a larger EOZ/POZ than FS-LASIK. Within commonly used ranges, POZ showed no independent association with EOZ/POZ. …
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: The effective optical zone (EOZ) after corneal refractive surgery is a critical determinant of postoperative visual quality, yet its magnitude and determinants remain variably reported. This study aimed to systematically compare the EOZ after small-incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) and flap-based femtosecond laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (FS-LASIK) for myopia or myopic astigmatism, and to identify factors associated with EOZ. METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA-compliant, PROSPERO-registered systematic review and meta-analysis (CRD420251075330). MEDLINE, CENTRAL, EMBASE, ClinicalTrials.gov, and WHO ICTRP were searched (January 2003-June 2025). Eligible randomized, nonrandomized, or cohort studies enrolled adults undergoing SMILE or FS-LASIK with reported EOZ. refractive.title: Unlocking Smiles: Evaluating the Diagnostic Accuracy, Reliability, and Acceptability of a Virtual Oral Health Screening Model for Caries Detection for Young People in Custody in Australia.
refractive.summary: Smartphone-based virtual oral health screening model was feasible and highly acceptable to end-users. This novel approach offers an acceptable diagnostic performance comparable to visual dental examination, making it a suitable population-based screening and triage tool for improving equitable access to oral health for all young people in …
refractive.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy, reliability and acceptability of a smartphone-based virtual oral health screening model for dental caries detection among young people in custody, using visual dental examination by a dentist as the reference standard. METHODS: A prospective cross-sectional study was conducted at two Youth Justice Centres in New South Wales, Australia. Young males aged 16-21 years underwent smartphone-based intraoral photography by a trained non-dental researcher, immediately followed by visual dental examination by a dentist. Two remote dentists, blinded to the results, independently reviewed the intraoral photographs. Primary outcomes were the diagnostic accuracy, inter- and intra-rater reliability, and end-user acceptability. Secondary outcomes included caries experience and the proportion of untreated decay. refractive.title: Early Postoperative Dry Eye Following ICL Implantation Versus KLEx for Moderate-to-High Myopia.
refractive.summary: Both procedures induced transient dry eye changes that largely resolved within 3 months. In this nonrandomized cohort, symptoms and tear film stability returned to baseline earlier after ICL than after KLEx, although the longer corticosteroid course after KLEx may have contributed. CFS correlated consistently with subjective symptoms.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare early postoperative dry eye outcomes after implantable collamer lens (ICL) implantation versus keratorefractive lenticule extraction (KLEx) for moderate-to-high myopia. SETTING: Yichang Aier Eye Hospital, Hubei, China. DESIGN: Prospective, nonrandomized study. METHODS: Patients with moderate-to-high myopia who underwent KLEx (n=96) or ICL implantation (n=64) were recruited. Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI), noninvasive tear break-up time (NIBUT), corneal fluorescein staining (CFS), Schirmer I test, and ocular surface analysis were performed preoperatively and at 1 week, 1 month, and 3 months postoperatively. Longitudinal changes were analyzed using generalized estimating equations (OSDI, NIBUT, CFS) or repeated-measures ANOVA (Schirmer I test). refractive.title: Cardiovascular Outcomes Following Smartwatch Irregular Rhythm Notification: Findings From the Apple Heart Study.
refractive.summary: Receipt of a smartwatch IRN was associated with higher odds of subsequent self-reported cardiovascular events beyond atrial fibrillation. These findings suggest that IRNs may identify individuals at elevated short-term cardiovascular risk.
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Smartwatch irregular rhythm notifications (IRNs) can identify atrial fibrillation. IRNs' association with broader cardiovascular outcomes is unclear. We evaluated whether receipt of an IRN in the AHS (Apple Heart Study) was associated with subsequent self-reported cardiovascular events. METHODS: We performed a post hoc analysis of the AHS, a prospective trial in the United States. Participants were enrolled via an iPhone app from 2017 to 2018; those who completed the end-of-study survey were included. The exposure was IRN receipt. Outcomes were self-reported new heart failure, myocardial infarction, stroke/transient ischemic attack, pulmonary embolism, and a composite of these events (major adverse cardiovascular events). Multivariable-adjusted logistic regression models included age, sex, heart failure, hypertension, diabetes, prior stroke/transient ischemic attack/systemic

refractive.title: Vector Analysis of Surgically Induced Astigmatism for Individualized Superior Incision Selection in ICL Surgery: Real-World Outcomes of Corneal and Limbal Incisions Stratified by Preoperative Astigmatism.
refractive.summary: In this real-world cohort, stratifying superior corneal versus limbal incisions by preoperative WTR astigmatism is associated with satisfactory refractive and visual outcomes after ICL surgery. …
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the clinical outcomes of a real-world stratified superior incision selection (corneal vs. limbal) based on preoperative with-the-rule (WTR) astigmatism for implantable collamer lens (ICL) implantation and to characterize surgically induced astigmatism (SIA) profiles of these two strategies using vector analysis. METHODS: This retrospective real-world cohort study included 139 eyes with WTR astigmatism from 139 patients who underwent nontoric ICL V4c implantation through a 3.0-mm superior incision. Based on preoperative refractive astigmatism (RA), eyes with RA ≥ 0.75 D received corneal incisions to harness SIA for astigmatism reduction, while those with RA ≤ 0.50 D received limbal incisions to minimize SIA. refractive.title: Awareness and Utilization of AI-Powered Smile Design Software Among Dental Students: A Pilot Study.
refractive.summary: Background and objective Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing dental diagnosis and aesthetic planning. AI-driven smile design tools allow dentists to replicate aesthetic outcomes using facial and dental data. …
refractive.abstract: Background and objective Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing dental diagnosis and aesthetic planning. AI-driven smile design tools allow dentists to replicate aesthetic outcomes using facial and dental data. However, implementation remains limited in Indian undergraduate dental education, particularly in resource-constrained regions. This study aimed to assess the awareness and attitudes of undergraduate dental students in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, toward using AI-driven smile design tools. Methods A cross-sectional pilot study was conducted among 30 undergraduate dental students in Thiruvananthapuram using a validated questionnaire distributed via Google Forms. refractive.title: Temporal and spatial patterns of corneal epithelial remodeling following wavefront-guided FS-LASIK and LASEK.
refractive.summary: Wavefront-guided FS-LASIK and LASEK exhibit distinct early regional epithelial remodeling trajectories that diminish over time. No statistically significant regional ET differences were detected at 6 months, although the reduced follow-up sample limits conclusions regarding complete convergence. …
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare corneal epithelial remodeling across a 9-mm corneal diameter following wavefront-guided femtosecond laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (FS-LASIK) and laser-assisted subepithelial keratomileusis (LASEK), and to investigate its relationship with postoperative refractive outcomes and preoperative ocular characteristics. METHODS: This prospective observational study included 153 eyes of 81 patients undergoing myopic correction with wavefront-guided FS-LASIK (90 eyes) or LASEK (63 eyes). Corneal epithelial thickness (ET) was measured preoperatively and at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively using widefield spectral-domain optical coherence tomography. Regional ET changes were analyzed across the central, paracentral, midperipheral, and peripheral cornea. refractive.title: Is the Seldinger Technique Safe for Level 2 Temporomandibular Joint Arthroscopy? A Retrospective Comparative Cohort Study.
refractive.summary: The Seldinger technique demonstrated a comparable safety profile to the conventional trocar technique for TMJ arthroscopy, with no significant difference in complication rates between techniques. These findings support the Seldinger technique as a safe alternative for TMJ arthroscopic access.
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ) arthroscopy is a minimally invasive treatment for intra-articular TMJ pathology but has a steep learning curve associated with complications. The Seldinger technique uses guidewire-based access and sequential dilation but its safety in TMJ arthroscopy has not been established. PURPOSE: To compare the safety, measured by complication rate, of a Seldinger technique with the conventional trocar technique for TMJ arthroscopy. STUDY DESIGN, SETTING, SAMPLE: Retrospective cohort study at Massachusetts General Hospital. Eligible subjects received level 2 TMJ arthroscopy for intraarticular pain and dysfunction between March 2022 and June 2025 and were >18 years. refractive.title: A privacy-preserving, ethically governed blockchain-digital twin framework for auditable molecular comparison and biocomponent provenance recording.
refractive.summary: This proof-of-concept provides a formal foundation for auditable molecular comparison and traceable biocomponent records. Molecular similarity alone does not establish transfusion compatibility or clinical safety; experimental and clinical validation remain necessary before clinical application.
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Convalescent plasma and other biocomponent transfusions offer rapidly deployable interventions against emerging infectious diseases. However, their use is constrained by adverse-reaction risks and the absence of a shared, tamper-evident record of previously compared donor compositions and associated outcomes. OBJECTIVE: To develop a privacy-preserving, ethically governed blockchain-digital twin proof-of-concept for auditable molecular comparison and biocomponent provenance recording. METHODS: Digital-twin representations of plasma, serum and related biocomponents were instantiated using chemical formulae, SMILES strings and sequence data retrieved from ChEMBL release 33 (2023). These representations were maintained in a relational working store connected to a permissioned, Ethereum-compatible Proof-of-Authority ledger. refractive.title: Assessment of Ebola virus persistence in vitreous fluid of Ebola virus disease survivors with vitreoretinal disease in Sierra Leone: a cross-sectional study.
refractive.summary: BACKGROUND: Uveitis is a known ocular manifestation in individuals who have survived Ebola virus disease (EVD). However, whether Ebola virus (EBOV; Orthoebolavirus zairense) persistence in vitreous fluid contributes to long-term sequelae of uveitis in EVD survivors remains unclear. …
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Uveitis is a known ocular manifestation in individuals who have survived Ebola virus disease (EVD). However, whether Ebola virus (EBOV; Orthoebolavirus zairense) persistence in vitreous fluid contributes to long-term sequelae of uveitis in EVD survivors remains unclear. We aimed to characterise the clinical findings and molecular and immunological findings in vitreous fluid from EVD survivors undergoing vitreoretinal surgery. METHODS: This cross-sectional study recruited EVD survivors (cohort 1), household close contacts of EVD survivors (cohort 2), and non-EVD patients with uveitis (cohort 3) from the Sierra Leone Ministry of Health's Department of Ophthalmology or from the ongoing Sierra Leone Ministry of Health and the Lowell and Ruth Gess Eye Hospital Ebola Survivor Study (SMILE Study). refractive.title: From area under the curve to clinical readiness: A framework for AI-assisted ectasia risk assessment before refractive surgery.
refractive.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) models for keratoconus frequently report near-perfect discrimination, with pooled sensitivity and specificity approaching 98% when manifest keratoconus is separated from normal corneas. …
refractive.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) models for keratoconus frequently report near-perfect discrimination, with pooled sensitivity and specificity approaching 98% when manifest keratoconus is separated from normal corneas. These figures are increasingly invoked to answer a different, more consequential question: whether an apparently non-ectatic cornea can safely undergo refractive surgery. We argue this is a task mismatch rather than a performance shortfall. Three targets are routinely conflated-manifest keratoconus, subclinical phenotype and future post-refractive ectasia-with the evidence strongest for the target furthest from the clinical question and weakest for the one closest. Underlying this is a single methodological issue: the absence of a robust reference standard, or ground truth, appropriate to the surgical decision. refractive.title: Differential effects of KLEx, FS-LASIK, and T-PRK on the effective optical zone and higher order aberrations in eyes with high astigmatism.
refractive.summary: In the correction of high astigmatism, T-PRK resulted in the highest EOZ/POZ ratio and the least induction of vertical coma, while SMILE produced the most circular EOZ and the least spherical aberration induction. …
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare the effective optical zone (EOZ) and higher-order aberrations (HOAs) after keratorefractive lenticule extraction (KLEx), performed as small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE), femtosecond laser-assisted laser in situ keratomileusis (FS-LASIK), and transepithelial photorefractive keratectomy (T-PRK) in eyes with high astigmatism. METHODS: This retrospective comparative cohort study included patients who underwent SMILE, FS-LASIK, or T-PRK for correction of simple or compound myopic astigmatism with a preoperative refractive cylinder magnitude of 3.00 diopters (D) or greater. EOZ characteristics and HOAs were compared among the three procedures using Scheimpflug imaging at 6 months postoperatively. RESULTS: A total of 134 patients (156 eyes) were included in the analysis. refractive.title: Persistent Ocular Pain and Neuropathic Corneal Pain After Corneal Refractive Surgery: Epidemiology, Evaluation, Counseling, and Management.
refractive.summary: Persistent postoperative ocular pain should be distinguished from clinical NCP supported by integrated assessment. Care should combine evaluation for alternative and coexisting ocular pathology with characterization of pain features, sensory findings, topical anesthetic response, and psychosocial contributors. …
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To synthesize evidence on persistent ocular pain and neuropathic corneal pain (NCP) after corneal refractive surgery and propose a clinical approach. METHODS: Narrative review of MEDLINE, Embase, and Web of Science from inception through July 10, 2026. Broad pain and refractive surgery terminology was used because nomenclature is inconsistent. Human studies were prioritized, and preclinical evidence was identified as such. RESULTS: Reported frequency depended on outcome definition and ascertainment. Two reports from the same prospective cohort identified symptom-defined persistent or prolonged ocular pain in 11% and 18% of participants under different definitions, whereas the frequency of study-defined multimodal NCP has been prospectively estimated in one small single-center cohort. refractive.title: Innovative mHealth intervention providing sustained anticipatory guidance (zero cavity): Design, validation, user perception and effectiveness - A randomized controlled trial protocol.
refractive.summary: INTRODUCTION: Early Childhood Caries (ECC) remains one of the most common chronic conditions in childhood, affecting over 600 million children globally. When untreated, it can lead to severe pain, abscesses, difficulty in chewing that contributes to malnutrition, impaired speech, disrupted sleep, low self-esteem, social withdrawal, and po …
refractive.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Early Childhood Caries (ECC) remains one of the most common chronic conditions in childhood, affecting over 600 million children globally. When untreated, it can lead to severe pain, abscesses, difficulty in chewing that contributes to malnutrition, impaired speech, disrupted sleep, low self-esteem, social withdrawal, and poor academic performance, all of which diminish a child's overall quality of life. Although largely preventable, ECC remains highly prevalent because of delayed preventive care and low parental awareness. Effective health education needs to be consistent, accessible, and available whenever parents need it. Although current evidence indicates that anticipatory guidance is a proven approach, its long-term reinforcement through a mobile app has not yet been tested. This study aims to develop and evaluate the effectiveness of a mobile health (mHealth) applica

refractive.title: Assessment of quality of life following dynamic facial reanimation surgery in patients with facial paralysis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
refractive.summary: The overall certainty of evidence was low. Pooled data suggest that dynamic facial reanimation surgery may lead to meaningful improvements in QoL, smile excursion, smile symmetry, and eFACE score for patients with facial paralysis.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: Facial paralysis causes aesthetic, functional, and social impairments that significantly impact patients' quality of life (QoL). This article aims to quantify the improvement in subjective outcomes following dynamic facial reanimation surgery through a systematic review and meta-analysis. METHODS: A systematic search of the Cochrane Library, PubMed, and Embase databases was conducted for English-language studies published before March 22, 2026, in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. The primary outcome measures included the Facial Clinimetric Evaluation (FaCE) scale and the Facial Disability Index (FDI). Secondary outcomes consisted of smile excursion, smile symmetry, and the electronic clinician-graded facial function scale (eFACE). Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were subsequently assessed using the ROBINS-I tool and the GRADE framework, respectively. RESULTS: The review

refractive.title: Ocular Complications Related to Iris-Fixated Phakic Intraocular Lens Implantation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
refractive.summary: Despite overall acceptable safety, Artisan®/Verisyse® implantation is associated with measurable ocular complications and progressive ECD loss.
refractive.abstract: TOPIC: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the cumulative prevalence of ocular complications following implantation of Artisan®/Verisyse® iris-fixated phakic intraocular lenses in adult patients undergoing refractive surgery. Outcomes included postoperative ocular complications and longitudinal loss of endothelial cell density (ECD). CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Phakic intraocular lenses are widely used to correct moderate-to-high refractive errors. Available evidence on complication rates is heterogeneous and often limited to narrative reports, hindering accurate risk counseling and long-term clinical decision-making. METHODS: This study was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251150677). Eligible studies included ≥10 eyes implanted with Artisan®/Verisyse® lenses reporting postoperative complications. Risk of bias was assessed using desig

refractive.title: Database-optimized versus manufacturer recommended lens constants for the prediction of postoperative refractive error following cataract surgery.
refractive.summary: Lens constant optimization using the Veracity surgical planner can result in significant reduction in prediction error. Using these database-optimized lens constants over manufacturer recommended ones may improve refractive outcomes after cataract surgery for most types of IOLs and eyes.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare refractive outcomes when Veracity database-optimized (Dopt) or manufacturer-suggested (Mfr) lens constants are used to perform IOL power calculations. DESIGN: Retrospective database study across the United States. SETTING: Database-optimized lens constants (Dopt) were validated in an independent dataset from 268 surgeons. METHODS: This retrospective database validation study analyzed cataract surgery cases planned using Veracity between November 2023 and December 2025. Dopt, previously derived from user-reported outcomes through October 2023, were evaluated against manufacturer-recommended (Mfr) constants in an independent validation dataset. Eligible eyes had their predicted postoperative spherical equivalent (SE) calculated using anterior and posterior keratometry, Barrett Universal II formula, and either Dopt and Mfr lens constants. RESULTS: In total, 14,172 eyes f

refractive.title: Dissociation Between Corneal Haze and Visual Function Following Corneal Cross-Linking in Keratoconus: A Rasch-Based Longitudinal Study.
refractive.summary: Transient postoperative increases in corneal haze-related densitometry following CXL were not accompanied by deterioration in Rasch-derived VRQoL. Instead, person ability improved at 3 and 6 months. Densitometry was not independently associated with person ability after adjustment for time.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate longitudinal changes in vision-related quality of life (VRQoL) following collagen cross-linking (CXL) in keratoconus and to assess the impact of postoperative corneal haze on patient-reported outcomes. METHODS: This prospective, questionnaire-based study included 55 patients with progressive keratoconus undergoing epithelium-off CXL. The Keratoconus Outcomes Research Questionnaire (KORQ) was administered preoperatively and at 1, 3 and 6 months. Visual acuity, corneal tomography and densitometry were assessed at each visit. Rasch analysis using the Partial Credit Model was performed to derive person ability measures from KORQ responses for both the physical limitation and symptoms domains. refractive.title: Comparative Clinical Performance of Lingual Fixed Appliances and Clear Aligner Therapy for Esthetic Deep-Bite Correction in Adults.
refractive.summary: Lingual fixed appliances were associated with significantly greater adjusted overbite reduction than clear aligner therapy in this retrospective sample of adults with deep-bite malocclusion. Although overbite decreased significantly in both groups, the findings indicate a difference in the amount of correction achieved. …
refractive.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Adult deep-bite correction extends beyond orthodontic alignment because it directly influences anterior esthetics, incisal display, smile arc, anterior guidance, restorative space, and the interdisciplinary planning required for minimally invasive esthetic rehabilitation. Although lingual fixed appliances and clear aligner therapy are widely used esthetic treatment modalities, evidence directly comparing their effectiveness for vertical correction in adults and its potential restorative implications remains limited. Therefore, this study compared adjusted posttreatment overbite and selected cephalometric outcomes between these two treatment modalities in adult deep-bite patients. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Pretreatment and posttreatment lateral cephalograms of 38 adult deep-bite patients were analyzed: 19 treated with lingual fixed appliances and 19 with clear aligner therapy. refractive.title: Mapping the Oral-Nutrition-Brain Axis in Aging: A Scoping Review of Evidence Linking Oral Health, Nutrition, and Cognitive Outcomes.
refractive.summary: Background: Oral health, nutrition, and neurocognitive health are increasingly recognized as components of healthy aging; however, their multidimensional relationships and plausible biological connections relevant to Alzheimer's disease and related dementia (AD/ADRD) risk remain incompletely characterized. …
refractive.abstract: Background: Oral health, nutrition, and neurocognitive health are increasingly recognized as components of healthy aging; however, their multidimensional relationships and plausible biological connections relevant to Alzheimer's disease and related dementia (AD/ADRD) risk remain incompletely characterized. Objective: To systematically map evidence linking oral conditions and function, nutrition-related factors and biomarkers, and neurocognitive outcomes in adults aged ≥65 years, and conceptualize an integrative Oral-Nutrition-Brain Axis (ONBA). Methods: This scoping review followed Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidance. Five electronic databases were searched for studies published from 2010 through June 2025. Evidence was harmonized across oral and functional indicators, nutritional/metabolic/inflammatory biomarkers, and neurological and cognitive outcomes. Results:

refractive.title: Short-term comparative outcomes of toric ICL implantation versus femtosecond LASIK for myopic astigmatism.
refractive.summary: In this selected non-randomized retrospective cohort, both TICL implantation and FS-LASIK provided effective short-term visual and refractive outcomes at 3 months. FS-LASIK showed better short-term uncorrected visual acuity, predictability, and astigmatic precision, whereas TICL remained a valuable option for eyes with higher refractive e …
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare visual and refractive outcomes, predictability, safety, and efficacy of toric implantable collamer lens (TICL) implantation versus femtosecond laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (FS-LASIK) in patients with moderate-to-high myopic astigmatism. SETTING: Instituto de Ojos Oftalmosalud, Lima, Peru. DESIGN: Retrospective comparative cohort study. METHODS: Consecutive eyes undergoing TICL or FS-LASIK were assessed at baseline and 3 months. Outcomes included UDVA/CDVA, spherical equivalent (SE), refractive cylinder, safety/efficacy indices, and vectorial astigmatism analysis. Double-angle plots depicted scalar magnitude/axis distributions. Non-parametric tests were used (p < 0.05). RESULTS: 149 eyes (74 TICL, 75 FS-LASIK) were analyzed. refractive.title: Incidence of oral complications after urethroplasty with oral mucosa graft.
refractive.summary: Longer OMGs, often requiring multiple or atypical donor sites, are associated with a higher rate of donor site morbidity. Surgical planning should prioritize graft minimization and buccal-only harvests where feasible to reduce long-term complications.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate long-term donor site morbidity associated with oral mucosa graft (OMG) harvesting for urethral reconstruction and to determine whether graft length and the number of harvest sites correlates with complication rates. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 304 patients who underwent OMG urethroplasty at a single tertiary care center between January 2011 and December 2017. All procedures were performed by one of three senior reconstructive urologists using a standardized technique. Patients were stratified into two groups based on stricture length: Group 1 (≤ 5 cm) and Group 2 (> 5 cm). Donor sites included the buccal mucosa and, in longer strictures, the contralateral cheek, upper, or lower lip. refractive.title: Interpretable Graph Neural Networks for Structure-activity-based Prediction of Drug-induced Toxicity and Adverse Reactions.
refractive.summary: From a translational standpoint, because AttentionADR requires only a candidate molecule's structure, it offers medicinal chemists and pharmaceutical safety teams a low-cost, interpretable triage tool that can flag likely ADR liabilities during early-stage lead optimization, before experimental toxicology or population-scale clinical data …
refractive.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Drug-induced toxicity and Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs) remain major barriers to safe pharmacotherapy and often arise unpredictably. Existing ADR prediction models primarily rely on population-scale data, limiting early detection and mechanistic interpretability. METHODS: We investigated whether molecular graph topology combined with attention mechanisms could explain variance in SIDER ADR labels. Drugs were represented as molecular graphs derived from SMILES, enriched with atomic-level physicochemical descriptors and Morgan fingerprints. An attention mechanism quantified the relative contribution of graph substructures and global molecular features. The proposed model, AttentionADR, was trained and evaluated solely on curated ADR labels without using clinical text or omics data. refractive.title: Intraocular lens exchange for refractive surprise after cataract surgery.
refractive.summary: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Refractive surprise remains an important complication of cataract surgery despite advances in preoperative measurements, surgical technique, and intraocular lens (IOL) design. …
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: Refractive surprise remains an important complication of cataract surgery despite advances in preoperative measurements, surgical technique, and intraocular lens (IOL) design. This review examines the contributors to refractive surprise and the role of IOL exchange, including indications, alternatives, surgical considerations, and outcomes. RECENT FINDINGS: Even though cataract surgery generally achieves excellent outcomes, postoperative refractive surprise still occurs. Contributing factors to refractive error include ocular surface disease, extreme axial length values, prior corneal refractive surgery, limitations in intraocular lens (IOL) power calculation, and postoperative IOL position or rotation. refractive.title: Opioid-sparing Pain Management for Pediatric Alveolar Bone Grafting: Efficacy of the Bupivacaine-soaked Absorbable Sponge.
refractive.summary: The application of bupivacaine-soaked absorbable sponge at the iliac crest donor site is a simple, inexpensive, and effective method for enhancing immediate postoperative pain management in pediatric patients undergoing alveolar bone grafting compared with subcutaneous local anesthetic alone.
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: The iliac crest is the gold-standard donor site for alveolar bone grafting, yet donor-site pain often leads to increased opioid use and prolonged hospital stays. This study evaluates whether the adjunctive use of bupivacaine-soaked absorbable sponge in addition to subcutaneous local anesthesia infiltration provides improved postoperative pain management compared with local anesthetic alone. METHODS: Medical records of consecutive patients who underwent alveolar bone grafting between January 2023 and September 2024 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were grouped based on whether they received bupivacaine-soaked absorbable sponge with local anesthetic (sponge group, N = 28) or subcutaneous local anesthetic alone (no-sponge group, N = 38). refractive.title: A Clinical Classification and Decision Tree for Pontic Site Management in Resin Bonded Fixed Dental Prostheses.
refractive.summary: The management of pontic sites plays a pivotal role in achieving long-term esthetics and functional success in resin-bonded fixed dental prostheses (RBFDPs), particularly in the anterior region where smile harmony and facial balance are of paramount importance. …
refractive.abstract: The management of pontic sites plays a pivotal role in achieving long-term esthetics and functional success in resin-bonded fixed dental prostheses (RBFDPs), particularly in the anterior region where smile harmony and facial balance are of paramount importance. While RBFDPs represent a minimally invasive and highly reliable treatment option for single edentulous sites, soft tissue irregularities and volumetric deficiencies at the pontic site may compromise the final prosthetic outcome. The present article introduces a structured clinical classification and a corresponding decision tree designed to support pontic site management in cantilever resin-bonded fixed dental prostheses (CRBFDPs). The proposed framework is based on two readily assessable diagnostic parameters: defect morphology and defect extent. refractive.title: Effect of phaco-tip orientation during phacoemulsification surgery (TIPS) on endothelial cell loss: Results of a randomized clinical trial.
refractive.summary: In routine direct-chop phacoemulsification with adequate preoperative endothelial counts, bevel orientation (bevel-up vs. bevel-down) results in a negligible difference in one-month endothelial cell loss and infrequent intraoperative complication rates. …
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare corneal endothelial cell (CEC) loss, central corneal thickness (CCT) and intraoperative complications 1 month post-phacoemulsification using bevel-up versus bevel-down tip orientation with the direct-chop technique. METHODS: Design: Multicentre, triple-masked, randomized controlled parallel group trial. PARTICIPANTS: Adults (≥18 years) with cataracts. METHODS: Participants were randomized 1:1 to undergo phacoemulsification with either a bevel-up (n = 241) or bevel-down (n = 239) using a standardized direct chop technique; Main outcome measures: Mean difference in CEC at 1 month, adjusted for baseline CEC using analysis of covariance with the intention-to-treat principle. Secondary outcomes included change in CCT and intraoperative complications. Subgroup analyses were conducted by cataract grade and baseline endothelial cell density (ECD). refractive.title: Clinical Interchangeability of Total Corneal Astigmatism Prediction Methods: An Agreement Analysis.
refractive.summary: The AK and Barrett formulas are clinically interchangeable for TCA prediction, with limits of agreement falling entirely within established toric intraocular lens planning thresholds. The DL model exhibits systematic, yet consistent deviations from both traditional methods that demonstrate lack of interchangeability. …
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare agreement between total corneal astigmatism (TCA) predictions from a deep learning (DL) model and those from the Barrett Toric Calculator (Barrett) and Abulafia-Koch (AK) formulas. METHODS: In 100 eyes with corneal astigmatism, Pentacam HR imaging (Oculus Optikgeräte GmbH) was used to generate TCA predictions with the AK formula, Barrett formula, and a previously validated DL model. Agreement was assessed using Pearson and Spearman correlation, mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and Bland-Altman analysis. Clinical interchangeability was predefined as 95% limits of agreement within ±0.25 diopters (D) for magnitude and ±5 degrees for axis. Predictions were also decomposed into Cartesian X and Y vector components. refractive.title: Temporary KLEx Lenticule-Assisted Corneal Cross-linking in Thin-Cornea Keratoconus: A Case Series.
refractive.summary: Temporary stromal lenticule onlay-assisted CXL appears to be a feasible and promising approach for progressive keratoconus in thin corneas, with encouraging short-term stabilization results requiring confirmation in larger studies.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the feasibility, safety, and efficacy of corneal cross-linking (CXL) assisted by a temporary stromal lenticule onlay in patients with progressive keratoconus and thin corneas. METHODS: This retrospective single-center case series included 14 eyes of 14 patients with progressive keratoconus and a minimum corneal thickness of less than 400 µm. A stromal lenticule obtained from keratorefractive lenticule extraction (KLEx) refractive surgery was temporarily placed on the de-epithelialized cornea to increase corneal thickness before accelerated epithelium-off CXL (9 mW/cm2 for 10 minutes; total dose 5.4 J/cm2). The lenticule thickness ranged from 70 to 140 µm and was removed after irradiation. Patients were observed for 12 months. refractive.title: Comparison of Visual Outcomes With Different Ablation Profile in FS-LASIK for High Myopia Correction: Ray-Tracing-Guided Versus Custom-Q.
refractive.summary: Individualized surgeon-adjusted ray-tracing- guided FS-LASIK was safe and effective for correcting high myopia, although a mild tendency toward overcorrection was observed. Compared with Custom-Q ablation, it was associated with lower postoperative SA, particularly at larger optical zones.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare visual outcomes in patients with high myopia undergoing individualized ray-tracing-guided femtosecond laser-assisted laser in situ keratomileusis (FSLASIK) versus Q-value-adjusted (Custom-Q) FS-LASIK. METHODS: This prospective contralateral-eye study included 66 eyes of 33 patients with high myopia requiring FS-LASIK. Ray-tracing-guided treatment was performed in one eye and Custom-Q ablation in the fellow eye. For ray-tracing- guided treatment, the ablation profile was generated using a ray-tracing algorithm and subsequently adjusted based on manifest refraction. Follow-up examinations were conducted at 1 day, 1 week, 1 month, and 3 months postoperatively. Visual acuity, manifest refraction, and higher order aberrations (HOAs) were assessed preoperatively and postoperatively. refractive.title: Comparison of 1-Year Clinical Outcomes Following SmartSight Lenticule Extraction Among Three Different Astigmatism Groups.
refractive.summary: The 12-month follow-up data show that SmartSight treatments for correction of myopia and myopic astigmatism with the SCHWIND ATOS is a safe, efficient, and accurate procedure irrespective of the level of preoperative astigmatism. …
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare the clinical outcomes of three different cohorts for astigmatism after keratorefractive lenticule extraction using the ATOS femtosecond laser system (Smart-Sight; SCHWIND eye-tech-solutions). METHODS: In this retrospective, observational, non-randomized cohort study, 216 eyes from 129 patients treated consecutively with SmartSight lenticule extraction were retrospectively analyzed in three groups based on three different levels of astigmatism (low: 0.00 to -1.00 diopters [D]; moderate: -1.01 to -2.99 D; high: -3.00 to -5.25 D). Over all three groups, the patients' mean age was 27 ± 5 years (range: 18 to 39 years) and the mean preoperative spherical equivalent (SEQ) was -4.68 ± 1.94 D (range: -0.96 to -9.50 D), with a mean astigmatism of -1.87 ± 1.33 D (range: 0.00 to -5.12 D). refractive.title: Ramsay Hunt syndrome presenting as a stroke mimic: a case report.
refractive.summary: Ramsay Hunt syndrome should be considered in the differential diagnosis of patients presenting with stroke-like symptoms. Early recognition and prompt treatment are essential for improving patient outcomes.
refractive.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Ramsay Hunt syndrome is a late neurological complication caused by the reactivation of the latent varicella-zoster virus, leading to inflammation of the geniculate ganglion of the facial nerve (cranial nerve VII). It typically presents as the classic triad of ipsilateral facial nerve palsy, otalgia, and a vesicular rash of the external ear. However, atypical or incomplete presentations may mimic central neurological disorders, resulting in diagnostic delays and an increased risk of permanent facial nerve paralysis. CASE PRESENTATION: A 46-year-old man presented to the emergency department with slurred speech, headache, dizziness, and three episodes of vomiting, raising suspicion of an acute cerebrovascular event. refractive.title: A critical review of the progress and application of finite element models in corneal biomechanics.
refractive.summary: Corneal morphology and biomechanics are the primary determinants of visual quality. Accurate biomechanical characterization is essential for optimizing the outcomes of refractive surgery and managing pathologies such as keratoconus. …
refractive.abstract: Corneal morphology and biomechanics are the primary determinants of visual quality. Accurate biomechanical characterization is essential for optimizing the outcomes of refractive surgery and managing pathologies such as keratoconus. Finite element modeling is an established method used to simulate surgical procedures, predict mechanical responses, and investigate pathological mechanisms. This review evaluates the progression of corneal finite element models. Early work relied on idealized two-dimensional cross-sections or simplified three-dimensional shapes; today, researchers routinely build personalized, high-resolution three-dimensional reconstructions directly from clinical image data. refractive.title: Effects of FS-LASIK and ICL Implantation on Horizontal Phoria and Accommodation in Highly Myopic Eyes.
refractive.summary: FS-LASIK and ICL implantation produce different effects on refractive status, horizontal phoria, and accommodative function in highly myopic eyes. Overall, ICL implantation provides more stable postoperative refractive outcomes and binocular visual function than FS-LASIK.
refractive.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare the effects of femtosecond laser-assisted laser in situ keratomileusis (FS-LASIK) and implantable collamer lens (ICL) implantation on horizontal phoria and accommodative function in highly myopic eyes. STUDY DESIGN: A quasi-experimental study. Place and Duration of the Study: Department of Ophthalmology, the Affiliated Hospital of Guizhou Medical University, Guiyang, China, from April 2024 to February 2025. METHODOLOGY: Patients with high myopia, defined as a spherical equivalent (SE) of -6.00 to -10.00 D, underwent either FS-LASIK or ICL implantation. SE, distance horizontal phoria (DHP), near horizontal phoria (NHP), and accommodative convergence/accommodation (AC/A) were measured preoperatively and at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively. refractive.title: Lateral orbicularis oris botulinum toxin injection for lip widening: A risorius-orbicularis oris balance concept.
refractive.summary: Perioral botulinum toxin injection is commonly used to treat vertical upper lip lines, gummy smile, downturned oral commissures, and to produce a lip-flip effect. However, apparent lip width also depends on the functional balance between lateral commissural traction and circumferential lip closure. …
refractive.abstract: Perioral botulinum toxin injection is commonly used to treat vertical upper lip lines, gummy smile, downturned oral commissures, and to produce a lip-flip effect. However, apparent lip width also depends on the functional balance between lateral commissural traction and circumferential lip closure. This study introduces a lateral orbicularis oris injection technique based on the functional balance between the risorius and orbicularis oris muscles. A low-dose mucosal approach was used, with botulinum toxin injected at four lateral orbicularis oris points. On each side, a reference point was marked 0.5 cm medial to the oral commissure, followed by one upper and one lower mucosal injection point located approximately 0.5 cm from the reference point. refractive.title: Implantable collamer lens surgery for high myopia: safety boundaries, vault management, and patient selection.
refractive.summary: Posterior chamber implantable collamer lens (ICL) implantation provides additive refractive correction for selected phakic patients, especially those with high myopia and limited corneal laser options. …
refractive.abstract: Posterior chamber implantable collamer lens (ICL) implantation provides additive refractive correction for selected phakic patients, especially those with high myopia and limited corneal laser options. This narrative Mini Review synthesizes literature published mainly from January 2021 through May 2026 to connect patient selection with measurable safety boundaries, separate lens power and size planning, dynamic vault assessment, and long-term surveillance. It also discusses hyperopic ICLs, non-EVO lenses, alternative phakic IOL platforms such as IPCL, and emerging artificial intelligence. True anterior chamber depth, age-appropriate endothelial reserve, open angles, crystalline lens status, and refractive stability define eligibility. refractive.title: Comparison of Optical Quality After Q-Value-Adjusted LASIK, Topography-Guided LASIK, and Ray-Tracing-Guided LASIK: A Retrospective 3-Month Study.
refractive.summary: All three customized FS-LASIK approaches achieved favorable short-term visual and refractive outcomes. Compared with the primarily cornea-based approaches, ray-tracing-guided LASIK was associated with more negative postoperative spherical aberration and different postoperative corneal-internal ocular aberration relationships. …
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare the visual outcomes, refractive predictability, and optical quality of three customized femtosecond laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis (FS-LASIK) approaches: Q-value-adjusted (Custom-Q), topography-guided (TCAT), and ray-tracing-guided (InnovEyes) ablation. METHODS: This retrospective, nonrandomized study included 194 eyes from 110 patients who underwent FS-LASIK at Shanghai Aier Eye Hospital between January 2024 and April 2026. The eyes were divided into three groups: Custom-Q (n = 69), TCAT (n = 49), and InnovEyes (n = 76). Wavefront aberrations were measured using the iTrace Visual Function Analyzer at a pupil diameter of 4.0 mm. Compensation factor (CF) analysis was performed to evaluate the relationship between corneal and internal ocular aberrations. refractive.title: Physiological aging of the tear film: characterizing non-invasive breakup time dynamics by age and sex.
refractive.summary: Tear film stability decreases progressively with age and differs by sex, with females showing lower and more variable NITBUT. These findings support incorporating age- and sex-related factors into DED evaluation and management, and align with growing evidence that qualitative tear film changes contribute to age-related instability.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: This study assessed the relationship between age and non-invasive tear breakup time (NITBUT), and examined sex-related differences in NITBUT to identify age- and sex-specific patterns relevant to the risk and presentation of dry eye disease (DED). METHODS: This retrospective study reviewed clinical records of adults who underwent optical prescription fittings between 2016 and 2024. NITBUT was measured with the Nidek Corneal Analyzer OPD-Scan III in 570 subjects (287 males, 283 females) aged 21-69 years, with approximately six subjects per one-year age interval. Group comparisons and regression analyses assessed associations with age and sex. RESULTS: Mean NITBUT was 8.27 ± 2.15 s in males, 7.46 ± 2.45 s in females, and 7.86 ± 2.01 s overall, with males significantly longer than females (p < 0.001). refractive.title: Transforming Children's Oral Health Worldwide: Three Decades of the Colgate Bright Smiles, Bright Futures® Prevention Program.
refractive.summary: The Colgate Bright Smiles, Bright Futures (BSBF) prevention program is a global oral health program designed to improve children's oral health through integrated prevention, education, community engagement, and partnerships with public, private, and academic organizations. …
refractive.abstract: The Colgate Bright Smiles, Bright Futures (BSBF) prevention program is a global oral health program designed to improve children's oral health through integrated prevention, education, community engagement, and partnerships with public, private, and academic organizations. As Colgate-Palmolive's flagship social impact initiative, the program was launched in North America in 1991 and rapidly expanded to countries around the world in 1994. It has since been successfully integrated into and adapted across diverse local cultures, healthcare systems, schools, ministries of health, and community organizations. The program aims to improve oral health literacy, promote beneficial oral health behaviors, and expand access to preventive services, including free dental screenings and treatment referrals. refractive.title: Polypseudophakia with the J&J synergy lens in high myopia: case report.
refractive.summary: Further studies are needed to determine which patients can tolerate this procedure. Providers should proceed cautiously and anticipate complications such as UGH syndrome following secondary sulcus IOL placement.
refractive.abstract: INTRODUCTION AND IMPORTANCE: As clinicians strive to provide personalized recommendations for patients, polypseudophakia may be an option for those outside the range of traditional extended depth-of-focus lenses. We describe a case with initial refractive success but the development of a potentially vision-threatening complication. PRESENTATION OF CASE: A 40-year-old Asian man with high myopia presented for a refractive surgery consultation with a goal of total spectacle independence and underwent bilateral refractive lens exchange with the J&J Synergy lens in the capsular bag, and a minus-power Alcon MA60MA lens in the sulcus. Initially, there was refractive success with post-operative uncorrected distance vision of 20/20 in the right eye and 20/25 in the left eye at 6 months. refractive.title: Refractive surgery.
refractive.summary: Refractive surgery has evolved beyond laser refractive techniques over the past decade. Laser refractive surgery procedures (such as laser in-situ keratomileusis), surface ablation techniques (such as laser epithelial keratomileusis), and photorefractive keratectomy have now been established as fairly safe procedures that produce excellen …
refractive.abstract: Refractive surgery has evolved beyond laser refractive techniques over the past decade. Laser refractive surgery procedures (such as laser in-situ keratomileusis), surface ablation techniques (such as laser epithelial keratomileusis), and photorefractive keratectomy have now been established as fairly safe procedures that produce excellent visual outcomes for patients with low-to-moderate amounts of ametropia. Additionally, a broader selection of options are now available to treat a wider range of refractive errors. Small incision lenticule extraction uses a femtosecond laser to shape a refractive lenticule, which is removed through a small wound. The potential advantages of this procedure include greater tectonic strength and less dry eye. In the future, intracorneal implants could be used to treat hyperopia or presbyopia.
